#1964. I witnessed recurring Celtic Remembrance Sunday embarrassment but Green Brigade act commended

Despite some rocky results, Celtic have made it to another international break still in front of Rangers. They are four points clear of the second-placed Ibrox side, who have a game in hand, after a narrow 1-0 Remembrance Sunday win over Kilmarnock.

Parkhead is unlike most places in the United Kingdom on Remembrance Sunday. Before kick-off, as fans milled around outside the stadium, there was barely a single poppy visible.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

This was the 13th time since 1974, when Celtic first played a Sunday fixture, that they have been in action on Remembrance Sunday itself, the fifth time at home.

People wondered beforehand what would happen and whether a period of silence would be attempted at all. After all, when Celtic published their Kilmarnock matchday guide, including “everything you need to know about the game”, there was no mention of the day’s significance. All it advised was that supporters should be in their seat for the 4pm kick-off – put back due to Remembrance Sunday activities in Glasgow - to “make some noise for the Bhoys”. Well, many certainly managed this.

The Tannoy announcer stated there would be “some moments” of silence to commemorate the war dead. The Green Brigade opted to stay outside, which is to be commended. They clearly took the view that if others wished to take part in the tribute, then they could.

However, so many elsewhere in the stadium reacted by booing and jeering once John Beaton had blown his whistle to signal the start of the tribute that the referee swiftly ended. The ‘tribute’ was timed at just 13 seconds, which is some way short of the minute that is the norm on such occasions.

To be fair, the announcer had said the plan was for a "few moments’ silence" rather than a full minute. But there was barely even a few moments’ worth.

One wonders if Beaton had been given a recommendation by the authorities to wrap things up as quickly as possible if the booing started, because he did so almost immediately. Although it was an ugly cacophony, maybe it might have been better if he had just stood his ground and let it play out.

Others might argue it would have been better if the silence had not been scheduled – or attempted – at all. Everyone knew what was going to happen.

But then what about the Celtic fans who do wish to pay their respects – and there were plenty. And the Kilmarnock fans, small group though they were, had every right to expect to be able to stand and remember relatives who had made the greatest sacrifice.

The Green Brigade stayed away, which was fair enough. But many inside the ground, according to testimonies on Facebook and elsewhere, explained that they had wanted to observe a silence. The Celtic board have enough on their plate without seeking more aggravation. They are probably just happy that it's all over for another year. However, the vexed question of war remembrance is a recurring issue that embarrasses the club annually.

The issue of Kasper Hogh’s Parkhead goal drought dominated the post-match debate as did Mika Baur’s worrying ankle injury. So focus was not necessarily on the Parkhead return of Luke McCowan, whom many once wondered if they might ever see in a Celtic shirt again.

He was sent on in the dying minutes against Falkirk last weekend when Celtic were in dire straits. The stakes were higher this time. He replaced Benjamin Nygren with eight minutes left, and with Celtic desperate to hold on to a 1-0 lead. It was his first home appearance for Celtic since being taken off at half-time against Rangers on 20 September. You just can’t keep a good (Celtic) man down.

Some questioned whether he could ever recover from his disastrous cameo appearance against LASK in August as Celtic tumbled out of Champions League qualifying at the hands of their Austrian opponents.

After a few weeks in purdah, he started the league clash against Rangers just before the last international break. It didn’t go well. The midfielder was replaced at half time with Celtic trailing 1-0.

Might this stand as McCowan’s last appearance? Again, many assumed so. Tony Docherty, his former Dundee manager and now in charge of the Scotland Under-21s, recently mentioned on a podcast that the player was “having a tough time” having been bombed out of the squad completely.

However, the boyhood Celtic fan isn’t giving up on his Celtic career, that’s clear. Just as Hogh received warm applause when he left the field after 70 minutes, McCowan was greeted with similar when he was announced as coming on.

Admittedly, you feared for him slightly. Celtic were still hanging on to a 1-0 lead and it was getting increasingly nervy. One misplaced pass could have had dire consequence. But he was tidy and busy, and he even saw an effort slip through Nico Mantl’s fingers and into the net, although the whistle had already blown for a foul. Fans cheered, possibly slightly cruelly.

Who knows what it means for his Celtic future? Martin O’Neill didn’t broach the subject of McCowan specifically afterwards but he was asked about an unusual looking squad, which featured just one- goalkeeper Sam Johnstone - of the six late summer transfer deadline day acquisitions. Haissem Hassan, meanwhile, was a glaring omission. On this subject, O’Neill explained, slightly mysteriously, that it was all to do with squad “manoeuvring”.

#1963. First meeting against a team 20 unbeaten: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Ferencvaros

The first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros will take place at San Siro this evening in the Europa League.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

So, tonight’s contest is an unprecedented one, and it pits two teams together that have made very different starts to their Europa League campaigns.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match.

➤ Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencváros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026-27.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing.

➤ The Diavolo suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11.

➤ Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures.

➤ Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967-68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level.

➤ Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

#1962. Michael Carrick ‘pretty clear’ on Man Utd future despite relegation woes

Michael Carrick remains confident in his ability to oversee Manchester United’s resurgence after a “right mixed” three weeks left his team in the relegation zone and the head coach’s future under scrutiny.

The 20-time league champions will spend the November international break in 18th place as their wait to add to August’s solitary Premier League win against Ipswich continued against Aston Villa.

United showed spirit and all too familiar flaws as Sunday’s helter-skelter clash ended in a 4-4 draw after substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time following Tuesday’s 3-2 comeback win against Roma.

Carrick insisted afterwards that he would not walk away from a job that looked like it could be taken from him a fortnight ago and the international break provides an opportunity for the club to take stock.

Asked if the two-week pause comes at a good time for the group, the under-fire United boss said: “Yeah, it’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events.

“But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

“Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

“But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game.”

The final international break of the year would be a logical time for United to make a change given there is no free midweek until mid-December after returning with a trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Hearts set for six-man injury boost as Wouter Vrancken bullish over revival

Hearts crisis or just a bad week, is Vrancken in trouble and has Jamestown failed?

But Carrick is steadfast in his belief that he can lead the embattled side up the standings having seen enough positives since a 4-1 defeat at Como and 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth left his job hanging by a thread.

United failed to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off in a 2-0 loss at Chelsea, before Tuesday’s stirring 3-2 Champions League comeback against Roma was followed by the dramatic Villa draw.

“Goals change games, and you’ve got to deal with it, and it’s part of something we have to improve on drastically,” Carrick said.

“But there’s more than enough. We’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times.”

Carrick is far from perfect but has been let down by United’s transfer business in the view of outspoken defender Martinez and the fans who frequently aim chants at director of football Jason Wilcox.

Left-back was among the areas of need and Luke Shaw’s injury has seen Diogo Dalot often deployed there, but frustrations with the United full-back reached boiling point on Sunday as supporters cheered his substitution.

Head coach Carrick, who was unaware of United’s full-back then being hounded as he left the ground, said: “We’ve got to be careful with that, I think.

“I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We’re all frustrated. We’re all disappointed.

“The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that. Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions. He’s played left-back. He’s played really well at times.

“He gives a penalty away. He knows that, maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

“But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything, so I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group.”

#1961. Little Common hold heads high despite defeat to Roffey

Having suffered a heavy 8-0 defeat against the same opposition on the opening weekend of the season, Common showed just how far they have progressed with a resolute display that kept them firmly in contention throughout.

The visitors enjoyed the lion’s share of possession during the opening period, but Common remained organised and difficult to break down, restricting Roffey's opportunities despite their territorial advantage. When the visitors did find a way through, goalkeeper Matt Cruttwell was in fine form, producing two smart saves to keep the scores level.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

However, Common's resistance was finally broken on the stroke of half-time when a neat passing move from the visitors allowed Roffey to take a slender advantage into the interval.

The second half followed a similar pattern, with Roffey enjoying plenty of possession but finding clear-cut chances difficult to come by against a hardworking Common side.

Cruttwell was again called into action, producing an excellent save low to his left to prevent the visitors from doubling their advantage.

Despite spending long periods without the ball, Common continued to battle for every challenge and remained within touching distance of an equaliser as the contest entered its closing stages.

The home side's best opportunity arrived late on when Sam Ellis rose to meet a delivery into the area, but his header flashed across the face of goal and away to safety. It proved to be Common's final opportunity as Roffey held on to secure all three points.

Boss Russ Eldridge said: “I thought the lads put in a really disciplined and hard-working performance against a very good Roffey side. They are up near the top of the table for a reason and we knew we would have to work extremely hard without the ball.

“When you consider we lost 8-0 to them on the opening day of the season, I think today's performance shows how far we have come. We were organised, difficult to break down and, despite them having plenty of possession, I didn't feel they created too many clear-cut opportunities.

“It was disappointing to concede right on half-time because we had worked so hard to keep them out. We stayed in the game throughout the second half and always felt we might nick something.

“The effort and commitment from the players couldn't be questioned. We now need to build on these performances and start turning them into points. If we continue showing that level of determination and togetherness, I'm confident results will come.”

#1960. Scotland given major boost as key midfielder extends 120-day exile ahead of Nations League fixture

Scotland have been handed a major boost as they prepare to return to Nations League action after it was confirmed that Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka has withdrawn from the squad ahead of the team’s clash in St Gillen next week.

Xhaka, 34, has been forced to pull out of the Switzerland squad after picking up a calf injury in Sunderland’s 1-0 win over Chelsea in the English Premier League on Sunday, with the Swiss FA confirming he will play no part in their upcoming fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland this month.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Forced off just three minutes into the Stadium of Light clash, Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris confirmed he had been struggling with a problem before the game, his 50th for the Black Cats. “It looks like a calf injury,” said the Frenchman. “But we don't know exactly the timeframe at the minute. It was just the last sprint of the warm-up; that's often the case [with these injuries].

The news means that Xhaka, capped an astonishing 152 times by his country, has now been absent from international duty for the last 120 days. He also withdrew from last month’s reverse fixture at Hampden Park amid a pending investigation into claims that he forged a Covid certificate.

The Sunderland star was accused of obtaining a forged vaccination certificate for a doctor based in Lucerne in order to bypass travel restrictions. He later apologised and confirmed his actions were a result of “fear and uncertainty” and a “deep mistrust” in the vaccine, and received a suspended fine of £136,265 (150,000 Swiss francs) from the Lucerne public prosecutor's office. He voluntarily missed all four of Switzerland’s Nations League fixtures.

However, with the matter resolved, he was reinstated to Murat Yakin’s squad for their final two Nations League fixtures, including their clash with Scotland at the AFG Arena on Monday, November 16.

Needing just a point from their game against Slovenia in Maribor this Friday to confirm their status as Group B1 winners, it was hoped that their legendary captain could return to the national fold for the first time since their 3-1 extra-time defeat to Argentina in the World Cup during the summer.

However, on the eve of his side returning for their initial training camp, Xhaka’s absence has been confirmed by national team following a scan at the Academy of Light after he limped out of Sunderland’s win on Sunday afternoon. Revealing the news via a short statement, the Swiss FA said: “Granit Xhaka has to withdraw from the national team gathering due to a calf injury.”

#1957. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.

#1954. Bexhill are too strong for Billingshurst

It felt like a long time since the Pirates had travelled to Billingshurst in early August for the first game of the season, and a tough challenge on their sun-baked, dustbowl of a pitch, which saw Bexhill come away 2-1 winners. This was a chance to chalk up the first double of the campaign.

Prior to kick off, the Polegrove rang out to the haunting strains of The Last Post as two minutes’ silence for Remembrance weekend was impeccably observed.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Bexhill certainly started with clear intent and on five minutes Luke Donaldson met a ball in at the near post from Ash Latuske and just failed to meet the target. Minutes later Latuske himself had a shot well saved by Trigwell in the Billingshurst goal.

Quarter of an hour in and Jack Shonk burst through on the run but clipped his shot wide. It felt like Bexhill needed to capitalise on the pressure they were creating and convert one of their chances and on 25 minutes the opening goal came.

Billingshurst were all at sea from a corner and it was Callum Brand on the spot to knock the chance into the net. Five minutes later Bexhill created a great chance to double the lead when Latuske swept down the flank and set up Connor Robertson who fired over.

But if Bexhill thought the game was in the bag they had another think coming as the closing phase of the first half proved to be the best part of the game for Billingshurst. Suddenly it was the home side on the back foot and with serious work to do at the back.

No game passes these days for the Pirates without Dale Penn being called upon to put his body on the line and on 37 minutes he threw himself across the six-yard box to clear a shot away at the death that looked for all the world like it was heading into the net.

It was a wake-up call for Bexhill as they went into the break and goal to the good. Attacking the favoured Brockley Road end in the second half they set about the task of putting the game to bed. But, again, they would have to be patient.

There was no shortage of creativity for the Pirates. And no shortage of chances.

On 55 minutes Trigwell pulled off the save of the day – tipping a Latuske volley on to the bar. Bexhill kept coming but were frustrated by some decent defending and it would be fair to say it was all Pirates in the second half.

On 85 minutes Theo Coombs, who had dropped deeper into midfield when Kyle Holden went off with a knock, got forward and drove a decent effort wide. A couple of minutes later Coombs got on the end of a great ball from Jack Mison and at last notched the second goal Bexhill had been chasing.

On the brink of full-time Charlie Scarles slapped the icing on the cake, breaking clear through the defensive line and tucking his chance calmly past the keeper.

A 3-0 scoreline was probably fair and gets Bexhill’s push to be contenders in the league’s chasing pack back on track.

On Saturday they are at home again in the league, with a 3pm kick off against Seaford Town.

Action returned to Palace’s final third, where Mac Allister attempted to fire home from a free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai forced a diving stop from Henderson, though the ball looked to be travelling wide.

#1952. Leeds United 1 Tottenham 0: Personality counts as Daniel Farke has everything that Roberto de Zerbi doesn't possess

Organisation, obduracy. Watching each other’s backs and sticking together.

Strong minds, intensity and feeding off the five-star fuel which is in abundant supply when Leeds attack the Gelderd End, particularly in the second half of matches.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

More especially when those present sense that one of the so called ‘name’ clubs don’t particularly fancy it on a November day in Yorkshire.

It was a win for the home dressing room and the culture that Farke has carefully constructed. He knew it - unity and commitment were the first two words he used to describe his side’s first victory in six games - and his Spurs counterpart Roberto De Zerbi also knew it too.

These are the sort of wins that proper managers love. Ones that are hewn from a bit of adversity. Conversely, they constitute defeats that tell a lot to the vanquished.

De Zerbi said that his side lacked ‘personality’ in the second half and he was spot-on. Personality counts in tight matches.

And while Noah Okafor may have only been on the pitch for just over a minute and a half before his match-winning strike 11 minutes from the end of normal time, nobody could say that the hosts’ breakthrough wasn’t coming or deserved.

Yes, Spurs were entitled to feel hard done by what happened - or didn’t - in the 37th minute with Mathys Tel. Ultimately that wasn’t the point.

A lengthy VAR check scrutinised Jayden Bogle’s challenge on the Spurs man close to the near touchline. The Leeds defender’s left-boot raked the back of Tel’s Achilles, leaving the Frenchman writhing in agony for a short while. Briefly, he did manage to continue before succumbing. Tel left Elland Road in a protective boot and on crutches.

In a post on X, the Premier League Match Centre later confirmed Bogle’s action was viewed as accidental and at low speed. It spared him from a red card, despite seemingly setting a precedent, as similar recent challenges from Jean-Phillipe Mateta and Ryan Sessegnon were deemed sending-off offences.

Spurs submitted a subsequent complaint to Pro Ref following the latest incident. But it was not the reason why they lost. Saturday served as a reminder that when things don’t go in the direction that you like, you show character and crack on.

In the second half, a group of players - several brought in at considerable expense in the summer - lacked cojones, as the Spanish say.

De Zerbi might be Italian, but he wouldn’t need to be told what it meant. He is still finding out about his group as a collective. Farke knows everything about his own and implicitly trusts them.

His Leeds side weren’t bad in the first half, but they weren’t particularly good either. Spurs possessed more of the poise on show. Mateus Fernandes - rightly cleared of a handball offence by an early VAR check - was prominent.

Seeking a fourth successive Premier League win for the first time in over 1,000 days, the visitors laid a decent platform without forging a lead in the opening half.

The second half was a different story. Leeds’ senior professionals in the likes of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ethan Ampadu took over.

Their eyes lit up and sensed Spurs uncertainty, while the unforgiving Leeds crowd reminded the visitors of their location south of the Watford Gap. Soft was the polite word employed.

Unlike those in white, the ones in indigo couldn't get going. Leeds, for whom Melvin Bard made an excellent impression after coming on for Gabriel Gudmundsson (hamstring) starred to become incessant in a half when they posted 13 goal attempts.

Nico Elvedi headed a rebound wide after Calvert-Lewin caused consternation. Ao Tanaka spurned a terrific chance, while Antonin Kinsky later made a splendid reaction save to tip over a hooked effort from the recalled Sean Longstaff.

De Zerbi had made a treble change to try and change the narrative. Farke played the telling cards.

Bard's throw-in on the left was flicked on by Calvert-Lewin. Replacement Harry Wilson challenged Rodrigo Bentancur and the ball dropped invitingly for Okafor, who did the rest. On the pitch for just 97 seconds, it was the quickest goal by a top-flight substitute this season.

The number for Spurs to mull over was 51 - the amount of Premier League games in which they have failed to win after going behind.

The late onslaught never came, although James Trafford made one key late save to deny Jan Paul van Hecke. After Bournemouth, that was important.

Leeds United: Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle (Rodon 93), Ampadu, Longstaff (Greuv 93), Tanaka (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson (Bard HT); Nmecha (Okafor 77), Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes unused: Zetterer, James, Aaronson, Bijol.

Tottenham Hotspur: Kinsky; Porro (Gallagher 65), Van Hecke, Van der Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes (Bentacur 65), Gray; Kudus (Williams-Barnett 83), Tel (Solanke 43); Marmoush (Kulusevski 65). Substitutes unused: Gunter, Senesi, Maddison, Davies.

One thing is certain: Tom Barnes leaves with the gratitude and respect of the Rustington faithful, while Darren Prior begins a new chapter with the backing of the club.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Sunderland ended their winless run in the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats entered Sunday’s game on a worrying run of form, with Thursday night’s Europa League loss to Dinamo Zagreb the latest setback, but an energetic first-half display against the Blues was rewarded when Enzo Le Fee scored from the penalty spot.

Chelsea enjoyed the bulk of possession after the break but struggled to make it count as they slipped to a fourth league defeat of the season and dropped out of the top four.

Victory ended a long winless run for Sunderland, who had last taken three points in the Premier League against Fulham back in August. They remain in the relegation zone but at least climbed off the foot of the table.

Regis Le Bris made eight changes from the Dinamo defeat, which included a first league start of the season for Chemsdine Talbi, while Chelsea made two switches from last weekend’s win over Manchester United as former Black Cat Jordan Henderson started.

Sunderland were handed a blow just four minutes into the match when captain Granit Xhaka was forced off and Jules Ahoka came on.

An even-paced start saw Ahoka win the ball and play Talbi through. The winger’s cross was met by Trai Hume, who had a hooked strike blocked by the defence.

Talbi was at the heart of another promising chance, sending in a great cross for Brian Brobbey, who volleyed wide.

At the other end Cole Palmer charged into the area and was bundled over, but a VAR check deemed contact happened outside the box.

#1949. GdS: Milan’s €500m Adidas deal causes reaction from rivals Inter – the situation

Inter are looking enviously at their city rivals AC Milan once again after Saturday’s derby, with the news of the record Adidas deal emerging.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport on Wednesday, under the new agreement Adidas will pay Milan €50m per year for ten seasons starting from 2028-29. This is when the collaboration with PUMA ends, who currently pay €24.5m per year, as per the last accounts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The paper (via Calciomercato.com) go on to state that it is likely that the €50m yearly figure includes sporting bonuses, such as participation in the Champions League, the value of material supplies (value in kind) and a portion to be invested in promotional activities (marketing fund).

Contracts with kit makers are not limited to recognising the value of just the home, away, third and other shirts, but can extend to the sale of related products. Then, guaranteed minimums and royalties come into play that are triggered above a certain turnover threshold.

For example, in addition to the €24.5m from PUMA, €55.8m in revenues came from store, e-commerce and merchandising/licensing activities, in particular those relating to the contract with the same German company and those from licensing with Fanatics and MatchWornShirt.

As for Inter, the renewal with Nike – effective from 2023 – resulted in a 70% increase over the previous contract, but the €28m per year is not in line with the club’s current commercial value. In addition to the Milan-Adidas deal, Juventus currently get €46m per year from Adidas (€41m from 2027-28).

Inter have maintained their merchandising revenues internally, over €35m in 2025-26 thanks to the new business model introduced with Fanatics, but Nike’s €28m is too little according to the Nerazzurri’s commercial management.

The contract expires in 2031, and La Gazzetta report that they will seek to renegotiate the deal to avoid accumulating delays over the next five years. Considering that Juventus and Milan have committed to the next decade, Inter have leverage as the only one of the ‘big three’ up for grabs.

#1948. Leeds United boss Daniel Farke's delight at ending Premier League hoodoo plus Noah Okafor admission

Beforehand, United held the Premier League record for the longest run of games without a win before 3pm.

At the 22nd attempt, Leeds ended that unwanted sequence - which had stretched back to March 2022 - thanks to Noah Okafor's 79th-minute winner.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Farke, whose side also won for the first time in six league matches, said: "This talking point with this lunch-time kick-off is now out of the way. I quite like that as well, so that at least talking about it is a bit away now.

"You can win and lose some momentum pretty quickly. We have not done too much wrong in the past weeks, with just a very difficult spell of difficult away games.

"And then one home game against Man United, where it was actually a joke that we didn't win. So we didn't do much badly, but all of a sudden you have a few games in a row where you don't have the winning feeling and this is always difficult.

"To win back the momentum, the first win isn't about going out and playing the opponent out of the park. You have to earn and work for it and I think it was exactly the right way with this hard-fought and well-deserved win to win the momentum back.

Match-winner Okafor scored just 97 seconds after entering the fray. It was the fastest Premier League goal scored by a substitute this term.

On the impact of Okafor, who had been struggling with an abductor issue in recent weeks, Farke said: "Credit to our medical department and also to Noah, he has worked in a very, very disciplined fashion, 24 hours a day more or less to be available.

"With a few concerns of the medical department, they said (on Friday): 'Boss, Listen, if you want to use him, you have to make sure that you stay unbelievably disciplined and you can't bring him on longer than 15 or 20 minutes.'

On Gabriel Gudmundsson, who came off with a hamstring injury at the break, Farke added: "I hope that it's not too bad and hope to have him back on the other side of the international break."

#1947. Xabi Alonso knows he has at least one Chelsea dependable

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

When Emmanuel Emegha came on in the 87th minute to join Danny Welbeck up front, the only surprising thing, as Chelsea got desperate in their bid to save themselves at the last at Sunderland, was that it was Jordan Henderson to make way.

Henderson was unlikely to provide the goal threat Chelsea needed in those dying embers of Sunday’s eventual 1-0 defeat, but he had increasingly been the free man and the right passing option for whoever in yellow and black had the ball at their feet as the match had gone on.

A defeat at the Stadium of Light to the side who had begun the day at the bottom of the Premier League table was a grim result for Xabi Alonso’s team to head into the international break with, especially given it was reminiscent of the 3-0 loss at Brentford ahead of the last hiatus.

Chelsea were devoid of ideas and lacking any semblance of the sort of control Alonso has publicly called for from his players.

And yet whatever it is about his team that is failing to give him that control and dominance right now, the problem is to be found elsewhere than where Henderson is going about his business.

Though they won last weekend against Manchester United without him, his return at Sunderland following illness was a welcome one. A midfield of Moises Caicedo plus either Romeo Lavia or Henderson or both, as was deployed on Sunday, is just about the only thing functioning as it should be for Chelsea right now.

For Henderson personally, it was a full-circle afternoon in the North East. Henderson is Sunderland born and bred and his appearance was significant. It was for Sunderland, against Chelsea, that 18 years and seven days earlier he had made his senior debut. Now came the 700th appearance, donning the colours of the visiting team.

Chelsea pay the penalty in latest defeat to Sunderland

The visitors faltered. With a controversial penalty given against them and Cole Palmer contentiously not awarded one of his own, Palmer and Morgan Rogers both had off-days, Levi Colwill was deemed expendable enough to be substituted at half-time, and none of Alonso’s substitutions could force the issue and muster an equaliser.

Henderson was sensible in possession when others around him were not

Henderson, though, was sensible in possession when others around him were not. He kept the ball moving, with one-touch passes into feet, relieving the pressure Chelsea were under in one of English football’s more hostile grounds.

Alonso won all five games against Sunderland as a Liverpool player and scored the winner in one of them, yet no such Midas touch in Chelsea colours from the technical area this time. His Chelsea gave Sunderland their first win in eight Premier League matches.

Winning blockbuster battles against the so-called ‘big six’ is important, but Premier League titles are won and European places earned by finding consistency, by winning home and away against the Sunderlands, Hulls and Fulhams of the Premier League.

Chelsea are yet to reach that point, as Henderson — who spent years in Liverpool teams that could and did — will be all too aware. The 36-year-old is not the problem. He actually represents what there is that’s working.

#1946. 'Kaoru Mitoma and Stefanos Tzimas' - Brighton issue injury update and expected timeline for returns

Fabian Hurzeler is hopeful his high-flying Brighton side will be further boosted by the return of long-term absentees Kaoru Mitoma and Stefanos Tzimas after the international break.

Yankuba Minteh made his first Premier League appearance of the season following an ankle problem by coming off the bench in Sunday’s 2-0 win over Brentford as the Seagulls moved second in the table.

Fellow winger Mitoma has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury in May, while forward Tzimas tore his ACL in December last year.

Asked if Mitoma, 29, could be involved away to Hull on Sunday, November 22, head coach Hurzeler said: “There’s big hope and big belief that this will be the case but it might be that we need one or two weeks longer, so I can’t say this is the game he will be back.

“We give him the time he needs and we know that if he’s back on his highest level he will be very important for us.”

Speaking of 20-year-old Tzimas, Hurzeler said: “He’s a little bit further than Kaoru (in his rehabilitation). He seems to be on a really good level.

“He was training when we were away (during a run of five successive away matches before the Brentford match), the same like Kaoru, and I see him back on the pitch with the team after the international break.”

Pascal Gross sealed victory over Brentford by converting a penalty to add to Diego Gomez’s stunning strike but insisted Brighton, who are five points behind leaders Arsenal, are not title contenders.

The midfielder told Sky Sports: “No, we are not in a title race. But we have started the season really well. We are not getting carried away yet. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this.”

#1945. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

#1944. Xabi Alonso disagrees with Chelsea player over controversial penalty decision

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso and goalkeeper Mike Penders disagree over Sunderland’s match-winning penalty.

The Blues suffered a painful 1-0 defeat to Sunderland on Sunday, losing to the team that began the day rooted to the foot of the Premier League table.

Enzo Le Fee scored the only goal of the game from the penalty spot after Levi Colwill was controversially adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey when tussling with the Dutch striker as he ran towards goal.

It came just minutes after Cole Palmer felt he should have had a penalty for a foul which officials instead believed was from contact initiated outside the box.

After the match, which left Chelsea fifth in the table, Penders gave his opinion on the spot-kick he had conceded.

“For me it wasn't a penalty,” he told Sky Sports. “[Colwill] barely touched [Brobbey]. I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.”

#1942. Thoughts of a lifelong fan: Where to start?

Where to start? Yesterday was not good enough. It wasn’t good enough from the players, the coach and yes, from some of our supporters too. When we arrived at Wimborne Stadium, after the half mile walk from the car park, spirits were high with some fans predicting an easy victory, whereas I would have taken a win on penalties if it had been on offer there and then. We all know we didn’t get that; we couldn’t blame the referee as none of the ref’s decisions would have affected the result, and we have to accept that on the day Wimborne wanted it more than we appeared to.

I hope you have noticed the use of “we” in my writing, because that’s what following and supporting any team in any sport should be about. I was at Old Trafford when we went a goal down and the level of support we gave increased, I was also at Wrexham when we lost four-one in the promotion season and were complimented by the Welsh fans on how we stuck with our team throughout the whole game.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The difference yesterday? Apart from some players giving their all there appeared to be no plan of action to get the right result. I can’t accept it was all down to the players though, as the coach would seem to suggest. I believe that we have enough quality players in our bottom of the table side, not to be where we currently sit at the nadir of the 92 and out of all the cups that really should matter to us. I believe that supporting a team must be shown more when things aren’t going right, and if that means cheering your team on even when they are losing to a poor side, who would normally be beaten easily, then so be it.

Nobody covered themselves in glory yesterday, the coach, players and us the fans.  Some of the “us” were too quiet whilst some chose to be negatively noisy, demolishing, rather than supporting the players on the pitch.

You can tell I’m not a happy devil, but will I be there at the next game to cheer the players on? Yes, I will, and I’ll keep on supporting them no matter what.

#1940. Barnsley FC and Daniel Stendel welcomed fun back like an old friend in FA Cup win v Aldershot Town - analysis

As Daniel Stendel sat down to dissect Barnsley’s 7-2 FA Cup win over Aldershot Town, he offered a wry smile.

He had been asked about the two goals his side leaked late in a game that had already been taken well beyond the opposition.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was a question he will have known was coming, and a question most managers would have enjoyed answering to demonstrate their forensic and demanding nature. The word ‘standards’ would have most likely been used.

Stendel, however, had no interest in poking holes in a mostly scintillating performance. And who could blame him?

Barnsley’s campaign has been largely devoid of fun and rife with simmering discontent. With Bonfire Night celebrations spilling over into the weekend, Stendel clearly felt the Reds needed to simply enjoy the sparks.

“We keep the positive things,” said Stendel. “It's normal that I think about the two goals, but I think we analysed a lot in the last couple of weeks about some situations, some games, and why we didn't win the game in the end.

“I think today is time to say ‘good result, we're in the hat for the next draw’.”

Barnsley flew out of the traps at a dizzying pace and the brakes were simply never applied. By half-time, Cameron McGeehan and Vimal Yoganathan braces and a Reyes Cleary effort had Aldershot dead and buried.

McGeehan completed his hat-trick after the break and Rylan Brownlie got in the act, with the latter rounding off the afternoon after Aldershot had twice hit back via Annisuis Lewis.

“It was good to see that we used the spaces that we get, and a goal after a set-piece.

“I think three goals after crosses was good, especially that. It's one thing that we try to change and what we train in training, why we said we have to cross more balls in the box. And yeah, it was good today.”

Toxicity has enveloped Oakwell in recent months and while it has not been Stendel’s doing, it is clear he is relishing the trickling return of some positivity.

His side’s hard-fought draw with Oxford United a week prior evoked nostalgia, memories of a first spell in which supporter connection was strong.

They did not require the same spirit against the Shots but bluntly, it was just nice to see some goalscoring fun. It is a pleasure with which the Oakwell faithful have not been well-acquainted of late.

“We needed this game,” said Stendel. “It's a good opportunity for everybody to prove what we want to do next week and to get some confidence in defence and offence for winning duels, try to do things, cross the ball early, and in the box you can score goals.

“We have tough weekends in the past, and I think it was good for everybody, for the mindset, for the training time next week, for the game, especially before the weekend game.”

Barnsley will host Oldham Athletic in the Jersey Mike’s Trophy on Wednesday (November 11) but it is clear Stendel’s primary focus is on the Brick Community Stadium. That is where Wigan Athletic will entertain the Reds in a battle of two of League One’s bottom four sides on Saturday (November 14).

A battling league draw followed by a thorough dismantling of an inferior FA Cup opponent represents a start - but it would take a league win for the phrase ‘turning point’ to be uttered with any conviction. At present, it can only be whispered.

“I think we play sometimes really well, but we get no points for that,” said Stendel. “You have to score, you have to defend.

“I think it's important that everybody looks for situations that you can score, not only our strikers.

“I think this is important, especially for the next weeks when we have some games against teams around our situation in the table, but also we talk a lot about our defence behaviour, we have to improve that, and I think it was a good step in the right direction today.”

Jamie Crellin's men responded positively, showing plenty of fight and determination.

After an even opening, the hosts took the lead in the 12th minute through October's player of the month, Ade Adeyinka. David Przybylo played him through the middle and, from around 20 yards out, he unleashed an unstoppable strike into the net to give Bridges an early advantage.

The remainder of the first half was evenly matched, with Roberts producing several good saves in the Bridges goal. At the other end, the energetic Villavicencio continued to cause problems for the visitors, particularly with a dangerous cross towards Reece Hallard, whose header from six yards narrowly missed the target.

With Bridges short of options on the bench and several players playing through injuries, maintaining the intensity became increasingly difficult. Brentwood Town took control during the final 20 minutes, but Roberts came to the rescue with two superb saves to deny Cerulli and Sears, while the Bridges players continued to put their bodies on the line to protect their point.

There was late drama in the 94th minute when Reece Hallard chased a ball through on the counter-attack, only for Cripps to handle it as the last man.

#1938. Will Manchester United sack Michael Carrick and who could replace him as manager?

Michael Carrick could be on the brink of the sack as Manchester United manager.

The pressure has been mounting on Carrick following a disappointing start to the season, and the situation took a turn for the worse this weekend as, without kicking a ball, Man Utd slipped into the Premier League relegation zone after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City.

While, Tuesday night’s comeback win over Roma in the Champions League allowed Carrick to survive another day in the Old Trafford hot-seat, the former midfielder will be aware that he is not out of the woods just yet.

Man Utd fought back from two goals down twice to draw at home with Aston Villa, so where does this leave Carrick?

As reported by The Athletic last week, United hierarchy held talks about Carrick’s future as head coach following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on October 25.

Carrick had been widely expected to be sacked at that point and then again after Man Utd were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea in the Premier League, a result that sent them crashing down the table.

However, it was agreed that Carrick would oversee the Roma and Aston Villa games before his situation would be reassessed prior to the international break.

Now, even though Carrick ended a nine-game run without a victory in thrilling fashion against Roma, pressure still remains as the first half performance on Tuesday night was a disaster and United could have easily found themselves three or four goals down at half-time.

Of course, the second half did prove that the players are playing for Carrick, so much so that Matheus Cunha went overboard in getting himself sent-off after turning the game on its head with two quickfire goals.

There’s an argument that Man Utd now have some much-needed momentum, but the calamitous fashion of Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa suggests there is nothing of the sort.

Will a draw against Villa would be enough? United go into the international break in the relegation zone and therefore Carrick’s position surely becomes untenable.

As per reports, Manchester United's football operations leadership, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox hold all the power with regards to Carrick’s future.

The pair were both in attendance at Stamford Bridge last weekend and at Old Trafford on Tuesday, amid reports of being involved in discussions over potential replacements.

Taking into account that Carrick held crisis talks with Berrada and Wilcox after the Bournemouth game, they would all - along with minority shareholder Sir Jim Ratcliffe - be expected to meet at Carrington following the Villa fixture.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are leading contenders to replace Carrick if he was to be sacked as Man United head coach.

Both are currently free agents after leaving Newcastle and the Germany national team respectively during the summer, but Howe’s Premier League experience may be the deciding factor if a change is made.

According to the Guardian, Howe is the current preferred candidate of Wilcox, but Nagelsmann is highly regarded by Christopher Vivell, Man United’s head of recruitment, to replace Carrick which means there is the potential of a power struggle at board level.

However, a spanner could be thrown in the works, with German outlet Bild claiming that Bayern Munich are interested in appointing Vivell.

Furthermore, in a boost for Man Utd if they end up pursuing Howe, they will only have to pay Newcastle a compensation fee of £6million.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has ruled himself out of the running despite being tipped to become the next Man United manager by Paul Scholes.

Antonio Conte has made it clear that he would be interested in a return to English football, but a move for Unai Emery appears unlikely with the Spaniard poised to sign a new deal at Villa Park.

Interestingly, Sky Sports have reported that United will NOT hire another interim manager should Carrick be sacked, suggesting a contingency plan is already in place should there be a need for an immediate change.

In an extraordinary twist, Didier Deschamps has reportedly turned down an approach over the Man United manager’s job, as more details emerge over the future of Michael Carrick.
