#1895. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1894. Paul Merson says Arsenal star has been ‘like a new signing’ after Hull win

Paul Merson reserved special praise for Martin Odegaard following Arsenal’s gritty 1-0 victory over Hull City, claiming the midfielder has been ‘like a new signing’ this season.

Arsenal had looked on course to drop points for only the second time this term as newly promoted Hull dug in and managed to frustrate their hosts, with Declan Rice coming close to breaking the deadlock on three occasions.

Noni Madueke also had his head in his hands after being denied by Konstantinos Tzolakis with the minutes ticking down in front of an increasingly agitated Emirates crowd.

But the pressure told with 18 minutes remaining of normal time as Tzolakis again kept out Madueke, only for Odegaard to pounce and poke the ball home on the rebound to cue rapturous scenes in north London.

The reigning Premier League champions preserved their narrow advantage to ensure they moved six points clear at the top of the table after Manchester City were stunned in a 3-1 defeat away to Nottingham Forest.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

High-flying Brighton – the only team to get the better of Arsenal – will look to close the gap to five points when they play host to Brentford later this afternoon.

‘You know Hull are going to sit ten behind the ball and make it very difficult,’ ex-Arsenal and England midfielder Merson said of Arsenal’s win over Hull on Sky Sports.

‘If you score early, you just go on and then win 3-0 or 4-0 and it would be a nice day at the office. That didn’t happen.

‘Hull defended very well and it took Martin Odegaard to break them down if I’m being honest.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Noni Madueke comes inside, hits a shot, it gets parried… he’s the first one to react and there’s two defenders in front of him, about four or five yards in front of him, but because of his reaction, he runs past them, he hits it, there’s a slight deflection and it goes underneath the goalkeeper’s arms.’

Merson felt Hull shot-stopper Tzolakis was the man of the match in a game which could later be seen as vital if Arsenal are to successfully defend their title this season.

He added: ‘Arsenal weren’t great but they won and this could be one of those games you look back on at the end of the season and go, “Remember the Hull game when we nicked it at the end”, but yeah, Hull will come away and think they did alright.

‘For me, the goalkeeper was the man of the match for Hull so that tells you everything. Arsenal weren’t great but it was a great result.’

Odegaard was once again the heartbeat of everything Arsenal did well to continue what has been an outstanding start to the 2026/27 campaign for the Gunners captain.

The crucial 72nd-minute strike took the Norwegian’s goalscoring tally to five in all competitions this season. He managed only one goal in 36 appearances last term.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly,’ Merson said of Odegaard.

‘He moves it quickly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’

Arsenal will hope to tighten their vicelike grip on top spot when they return to Premier League action against Newcastle at St James’ Park in a week’s time.

A tough Champions League clash at home to Borussia Dortmund awaits three days later, before Mikel Arteta’s men head back to the Emirates to face off against Manchester City in the English top flight.

#1893. “It’s about ambition, concentration, desire” – Amorim tears into Milan after Ferencvaros defeat

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim did not hold back on his team’s performance after the 2-0 Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros.

Milan needed a win having lost two of their first three games in Europe, and instead they responded with perhaps their worst performance under Amorim. Lenny Joseph’s second-half brace was enough for Ferencvaros to emerge with three points that their performance merited in truth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was made to rotate again with six changes from the win over Inter, but in the second half the likes of Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Mario Gila and Luka Modric all came on. The end result was the same: frustration and an inability to piece together the required quality.

Amorim spoke to Sky after Koni De Winter offered his opinion that it is a psychological issue for the team. The words from the manager were transcribed by MilanNews.

You issued a warning that today would be complication…

“There’s no explanation. There’s nothing I can say, especially about the first half. I don’t remember another first half like it. It’s about ambition, concentration, desire. We gave away opportunities, we gave away stupid gifts. We weren’t prepared to play football tonight.”

“It’s hard to explain. We simply weren’t ready to move from the derby to this other competition. When you play for Milan, you have a responsibility, and you can’t show up like that. I probably didn’t ensure the team took to the field ready either.”

De Winter says it’s a matter of mentality…

“We’re not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We need to work on our way of looking at football and how we approach matches. There are no excuses tonight, there’s nothing I can say.

“I usually have a lot to say in defence of our team, but not tonight. We need to be more humble and understand what happened.”

“Maybe I did something wrong these past two days, but not mentally. This team had similar problems last year. We have to find a solution. Tonight we weren’t ready, we weren’t brave. If we don’t win, we’ll have to do everything we can to turn things around, and we didn’t see that.

“Everyone needs to train like Pavlovic. He’s ready to die in training. He’s a good example. Sometimes when players don’t start, they struggle. But there are no excuses; we should have won even with those who started.”

“We have to fix this! We can’t just assume it’s going to be like this. We should have done so many things better tonight. Just being better on second balls would have been much better. We weren’t in the game tonight.”

How important is the Europa League now? It’s a complicated situation…

“I have to focus on the league, obviously, but we also have to do well in the Europa League. We must and can win games despite the rotation. We have to be ready – we’re not now – to play and win every three days.

“But I won’t give up on this competition. But as long as the mathematics don’t condemn us, we’ll fight in this competition as we do in the others.”

#1892. Grant McCann faces biggest test yet at Doncaster Rovers - Leon Wobschall comment

Last November, Grant McCann watched his side lose 2-1 at Lincoln City - to extend the club's winless run to nine league matches, serious territory for most managers.

Fortunately, McCann could count on having credit in the bank—Rovers' 1,693-strong support sang his name intermittently. That stoic patience was rewarded and Rovers eventually turned a corner.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Which brings us to the present. Rovers' travelling followers - many of whom would have been among the big away contingent at Lincoln - were in far more febrile and angry mood after seeing their side succumb to a pitiful FA Cup exit at Kidderminster Harriers on Saturday.

Damning chants of 'You're not fit to wear the shirt' and 'We turn up and why don't you' arrived. McCann himself got the treatment.

A chorus of 'Sacked in the morning' was aired with McCann booed at the end of an awful afternoon.

Forty-two places separated the two clubs in the pyramid ahead of the first-round tie at Aggborough. What made the 3-0 defeat all the more stark for Rovers was the fact that Harriers, mid-table in the National League, had won just once in their previous nine matches in all competitions.

And then there was what had happened seven days earlier when Doncaster again imploded en route to a wretched 6-1 reverse at an Aaron Collins-inspired MK Dons. McCann's side are currently just one place above the League One drop zone.

After Kidderminster, McCann did not shy away from his responsibilities - as he never does - and fronted up. For the second successive Saturday, he issued an apology to fans.

In his time at Rovers, McCann has been in tough situations before and come out on the other side. The Northern Irishman has consistently spoken about how he actually revels in being written off and uses it as fuel.

“I’m from Sandy Row in Belfast. I do not hide,” is something he has said on more than one occasion.

The break in Rovers' league schedule might just be timely. McCann and co must close ranks and come out fighting ahead of a critical Yorkshire derby double-header against Bradford City and Huddersfield Town. Their previous derby victory against Sheffield Wednesday is something that should at least inspire them.

Taking aside the Trophy trip to Rochdale, Rovers have shipped 12 goals in three matches. McCann brought his players in on a Sunday to go over mistakes following the rout at MK Dons. Worryingly, another dereliction of defensive duty arrived at Kidderminster, where his side lost duels all over the pitch.

Going forward, Rovers have had issues in terms of goalscoring and have yet to get a consistent tune out of several summer signings. Injuries have compounded matters.

McCann will need to draw upon all of his experience to change the narrative at a club he loves. Don't bet against him, but it will be his biggest Rovers test to date.

The fans don't have his back as much as they once did.

McCann enjoys a fight and it's just as well.

#1891. Michael Carrick told four players that will 'RELEGATE' Manchester United and cost him his job

Gary and Phil Neville both believe that Manchester United’s current defence will drag the club into a relegation battle.

Michael Carrick’s struggling side twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday, rallying back on both occasions to secure a chaotic last-gasp 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

Manchester United have now conceded 19 goals in just 10 Premier League games this season, leaving the Red Devils sitting in the relegation zone heading into the final international break of 2026.

Gary Neville was a guest pundit on NBC Sports for the draw with Villa, with the ex-Man Utd captain criticising the club’s recruitment over the summer.

After spending around £200million on overhauling their attack in the summer of 2025, United focused on rebuilding their midfield ahead of the 2026/27 season.

But Neville believes that the club should have spent more in order to also fix their leaky defence.

He said: “The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window.

“Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

“The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors. We all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in.

“They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.”

United have not signed a senior defender since bringing attack-minded wing-back Patrick Dorgu to the club in January 2025.

Gary’s brother Phil concurred, agreeing that United’s defence as it finished against Villa would end up relegating the club.

Phil also added that it will cost Carrick his job as United manager.

He said: “The back four that finished the game – [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Lenny] Yoro, [Ayden] Heaven and Dorgu – that gets you relegated.

#1887. Manchester United set for crisis talks with Michael Carrick 'sack decision imminent'

Manchester United are set to assess Michael Carrick’s position as the sack looms for the under-fire manager.

The Red Devils go into the November international break in the Premier League relegation zone following Nottingham Forest’s win over Manchester City and United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa over the weekend.

Pressure has piled on the former midfielder after a run of nine straight games withot a victory, which was snapped in midweek as they roared back to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

They were unconvincing against the Serie A outfit and then found themselves two goals down in both halves against Villa on Sunday, coming back from 2-0 and 4-2 down to salvage a point.

It was expected that Carrick would be relieved of his duties following the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth three weeks ago, which followed the 4-1 thrashing by Como.

He was kept on for the visit to Chelsea - which United lost 2-0 - and he then oversaw the Roma clash, with it being reported that the club hierarchy wanted to give the ex-England international until the international window before they reviewed his situation.

#1886. Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with familiar problem after Hull win

Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with an old problem that became so cliched that it was featured in a sit-com 18 years ago.

The Gunners beat Hull City 1-0 on Saturday in the Premier League, with Martin Odegaard scoring the only goal at the Emirates.

Any problem Arsenal are struggling with is not too serious as that win, followed by Manchester City’s defeat at Nottingham Forest, put Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the table.

However, Arteta was frustrated with Arsenal only scoring one goal and it not coming until the 72nd minute, despite dominating possession and producing 21 shots at goal.

Sometimes the inability to even produce a shot was the problem, despite having the ball in dangerous areas plenty of times.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

In a 2008 episode of The IT Crowd, Moss and Roy both try to ingratiate with football fans by learning the phrase: ‘The thing about Arsenal is they’re always trying to walk it in.’

Arteta seems to have a similar take on his team, accusing them of trying to score the ‘perfect goal’ against defensively-minded teams.

‘[We need to] be more efficient,’ the Arsenal manager said. ‘We are one against one against the keeper. That’s happened twice today. There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing.

‘So many shots that have been deflected, blocked. We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that’s it. And open, I think, the scoreline much earlier because obviously that’s going to change the course of the game.

‘We had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren’t efficient enough to do that. And then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box, insisting, insisting and insisting until we are able to break them down. And this is exactly how we won the game.’

Odegaard is Arsenal’s top-scorer this season with five goals in all competitions and three in the Premier League.

While Arsenal’s attack does not always penetrate as much as Arteta would like, the defence is incredibly reliable.

Another clean sheet meant the Gunners have conceded just five goals in 10 league games and have not conceded in 10 of their 17 matches across all competitions.

Centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes said: ‘If we don’t concede goals, we have a big chance to win games. We are really happy to have another clean sheet.

‘Like I said, when we have a strong team, a strong defence, we don’t concede goals. I think this season, how many is that? Ten clean sheets in the whole competition? This is our standard. We need to keep winning.’

#1883. Michael Carrick sends new message to Manchester United fans over Diogo Dalot boos

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has urged supporters “to be careful” with their boos after targeting Diogo Dalot during the Red Devils’ 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Man Utd fans watched on at Old Trafford as their side twice rallied back from a two-goal deficit in dramatic fashion, eventually sharing a point with Unai Emery’s visitors.

For much of this season, Dalot has been deployed outside of his favoured position of right-back, instead lining up on the left in the absence of Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

Dorgu has recently returned to enough fitness to be named in matchday squads, and when the Danish wing-back was brought on to replace Dalot on 66 minutes on Sunday, boos rang around Old Trafford aimed at the Portuguese defender.

A regular starter in an often-criticised defence, Dalot had given away a penalty right at the start of the second half, allowing Aston Villa to regain their lead.

Under-pressure United boss Carrick was quick to defend his player, however.

Asked about the fans’ booing towards Dalot, Carrick responded: "We've got to be careful with that, I think.

"I understand the frustration, I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We're all frustrated, we're all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

"Diogo, he gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions, he's played left-back, he's played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today.

“Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that's part of it, he's made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he's giving everything.

"So I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we've got.

“Picking a team and who plays the next game, that's a whole different decision, but it's a whole different game that we've got to look forward to now."

Tottenham can feel hard done by by the decision not to send Jayden Bogle off for his tackle on Mathys Tel over the weekend.

“He is extremely lucky, he catches him across the Achilles, high, we have this directive of 'above the ankle, or Achilles' and that falls under that line.

“We saw it with Ryan Sessegnon a few weeks ago with a similar tackle and [Jean-Philippe] Mateta last week.”

Former Spurs manager Tim Sherwood said that he “would not have been surprised” to see the right-back dismissed, while ex-Premier League striker Jay Bothroyd claimed that the tackle was “accidental” and that he did “not want to see red cards for those kinds of challenges”.

The Blues returned to London with nothing, though, with an Enzo Le Fee penalty the difference between the sides.

There was controversy over the penalty decision, with Levi Colwill adjudged to have hauled down Brian Brobbey, although it looked like both players were pulling the shirt of the other.

Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders hit out at the decision, telling Sky Sports: ‘For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.’

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Alonso was not singing from the same hymn sheet, telling the BBC: ‘I haven’t seen it back. Nothing to comment on the referee. It is something that is our fault. We could have done better.’

He added: ‘I think it’s an action where he can defend better. It’s our mistake.’

Alonso was impressed by Brobbey over the game, not just in winning the penalty, but felt his defenders could have done better against the big Dutchman.

‘From transitions out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances, he got the penalty as well,’ he said. ‘But we have been preparing for that, we have tried, we could have done better.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but when you defend better than we did today.’

Clearly the former Real Madrid boss did not like he saw from his defenders and he was also frustrated with what his forwards produced.

‘I think we didn’t deserve more than probably one point,’ he said. ‘Not much happened, to be honest. We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win.

‘We were against a low block we missed a bit of patience, a bit of quality, a bit of creativity on the last third to create more chances, you need to be more consistent to move the ball from one side to the other that we didn’t do good enough.’

It was suggested to Alonso that Sunderland’s physical superiority meant they could bully Chelsea, but the manager said: ‘Not bullied. There’s situations that we could have defended better. Situations that we could have had better advantages in attack.’

Defeat left Chelsea fifth in the table, while Sunderland climbed to 18th.

#1874. Michael Carrick responds to Man Utd relegation fears after Aston Villa draw

Michael Carrick downplayed fears Manchester United were in a relegation battle after a remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

United will sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League during the November international break after a thrilling 4-4 draw with Villa at Old Trafford.

Aston Villa twice led by two goals but Manchester United produced two spirited fightbacks to avoid defeat and potentially prolong Carrick’s reign as manager.

Goals from Brazilian winger Alysson and Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson put Villa 2-0 up inside five minutes but the hosts were level by half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans equaliser against his former club.

John McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead just after half-time and the visitors appeared to have the game wrapped up when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth on 53 minutes.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But injury-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw Manchester United salvage a point and avoid a third successive league defeat.

The comeback rivalled the one United produced in the Champions League against Roma during the week but it remains to be seen whether it saves Carrick his job.

Despite avoiding defeat, the Red Devils slip to 18th in the Premier League after ten games, their lowest position at the stage of a campaign since 1986.

Carrick’s side have also gone eight league games without a win, matching a run they have endured just once before in the Premier League.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I’m disappointed that we haven’t won the game,’ Carrick said. ‘We looked the better team for long parts of it and we’re making it difficult for ourselves with the goals that we’re giving away.

‘We’re not just giving away one, it’s two in succession that put us in such a difficult position. We did it the other night, we did it again today and have come back into the game and had a lot of the game, could have won it at the end.

‘So I’m disappointed we haven’t won the game. It’s just moments that we need to tighten up on. Individual moments where we’re giving teams goals that we don’t normally get.

‘If we tighten up that, there’s a lot of good in that performance. I thought we should have won the game. But conceding the goals we are is not helping us at all.

"That's not going to happen" 🗣️Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l

‘We have got to tighten up, it’s pretty obvious to say that. It’s giving us too much to do in games. But I thought we did a lot and feel that we should have won the game.’

Asked whether he feels Manchester United are in a relegation battle, Carrick added: ‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation or the results but we can definitely do something about it.’

Responding to Carrick’s post-match interview, former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said: ‘It’s obviously difficult for the manager. He’s under pressure, no doubt

‘He talks a lot but doesn’t say much. I don’t know if that’s a tactic. Like a politician. He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there’s things we need to work on.

‘But they better get moving on that. It’s the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren’t very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it’s just going to continue.

‘What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.’

While Manchester United slipped into the relegation zone, Aston Villa stay 10th after extending their unbeaten league run to seven games.

#1873. Roy Keane criticises Senne Lammens after Manchester United draw with Aston Villa

Roy Keane said the form of goalkeeper Senne Lammens is ‘hurting’ Manchester United after a thrilling 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Lammens endured another difficult game as Michael Carrick’s side conceded four goals at home to Villa.

The Belgian shot-stopper was nutmegged by Alysson inside two minutes and then could only parry a shot into the path of Nicolas Jackson who doubled Villa’s lead on four minutes.

The writing appeared to be on the wall for under-fire manager Carrick but United responded and were level at half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans’ strike against his former club.

Aston Villa once again opened up a two-goal lead early into the second half, John McGinn scoring a penalty before Leon Goretzka poked home the visitors’ fourth.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Manchester United scored two injury-time goals through substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu to avoid defeat and salvage an unlikely point.

Despite two spirited fightbacks, an eighth league game without a win leaves the Red Devils in the relegation zone heading into the November international break.

Former Manchester United captain Keane was left with wildly mixed emotions after the game, criticising the poor defensive display but praising the team for showing ‘a bit of fight and desire’.

‘There have been question marks over this team showing a bit of fight, a bit of desire,’ Keane told Sky Sports. ‘And as bad as the game was from a football point of view they kept going until the end.

‘We go back to some of the basics. The way they’re starting games, the way they’re coming out for the second half. There are things they can improve on.

‘When they were on a good run of results last year, the goalkeeper was doing very well, making a lot of big saves, he’s not doing that. Bruno was on fire, he’s not at his very best at the moment.

‘The goalkeeper has to do better. It doesn’t help if your goalkeeper isn’t making saves, that hurts the team a lot.

#1872. Leeds 1-0 Tottenham: Roberto De Zerbi sets unwanted 39-game worst as Premier League record exposes major Spurs flaw

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 15:20

Tottenham Hotspur's loss to Leeds United means they have failed to win any of the past 39 matches in the Premier League in which they conceded first (D9, L30), an unwanted record in the competition.

Spurs were hopeful of securing a fourth consecutive win in the Premier League, but they instead suffered a 1-0 defeat at Elland Road, with Noah Okafor scoring a late winner.

The result leaves the Londoners in 10th place with 12 points after 10 matchweeks, but they are only three points from 16th-placed Coventry City.

Roberto De Zerbi will be particularly concerned by his team's failure to find the back of the net after going behind, with the club having only scored 10 times in the top flight so far.

Opta data shows that Spurs have in fact failed to win any of their last 39 Premier League games in which they conceded first, their longest ever run in the competition.

39 - Tottenham Hotspur have failed to win any of their last 39 games in the Premier League in which they've conceded the opening goal (D9 L30); their longest ever run in the competition. Setback. https://t.co/0FfwlLIXO1

Though Leeds could have been reduced to 10 men in the first half, a possible VAR error should not distract from the fact that Spurs looked poor offensively yet again.

The Londoners produced seven shots to the victors' 16 on Saturday, and no player in the visiting team produced more than one shot on target.

Despite signing the likes of Omar Marmoush and Savio in the summer transfer window, De Zerbi's side have rarely offered any threat in the final third.

James Maddison's creativity has been missed, but his absence cannot explain why they have failed to score in half of their Premier League games this season.

Spurs have finished 17th in the Premier League in each of the last two seasons, so nobody at the club can afford to take safety for granted.

Tottenham could end the weekend in 14th place, and the gap to the bottom three could be as small as two points.

De Zerbi has not been able to eradicate all of the defensive mistakes that have plagued the Londoners, and given his players have frequently struggled in the final third, it would not be surprising if they battled against demotion yet again.

#1871. England confirm surprise Marc Guehi withdrawal with replacement revealed

Dan Burn has been added to the England squad as a replacement for the injured Marc Guehi.

The Manchester City centre-back was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with an injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest.

Guehi will now remain with his club over the international break and is replaced by the Newcastle United defender Burn. The 34-year-old last played for his country in the 2-1 World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina in July.

Burn joined up with the rest of the England squad at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground on Monday morning as Thomas Tuchel’s side prepare for Nations League group games against Croatia on Thursday and Spain on Sunday.

Burn joins Jarrad Branthwaite and Arsenal’s Ezri Konsa as the central defenders available to the German this month, though Bayer Leverkusen’s versatile 23-year-old Jarell Quansah can also play in the middle of defence and Tuchel says he is an option there if needed.

The injury Guehi picked up in the Forest game was a hip problem that saw him substituted at half time at the City Ground before undergoing scans over the weekend.

His replacement, Burn, has been a favourite of Tuchel’s for England, earning all of his 11 caps during the German’s tenure and making his debut in Tuchel’s first match in charge back in March 2025.

#1869. Gary Neville names four players who will ‘get Man Utd relegated’ after Aston Villa draw

Gary Neville has slammed Manchester United’s failure to sign any new defenders last summer and says the back-four that finished the remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa will ‘get the club relegated’.

The Premier League giants go into the November international break sitting 18th in the table after Villa twice blew two-goal leads to draw at Old Trafford.

United found themselves 2-0 down inside five minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson took advantage of the hosts’ fragile defence.

Michael Carrick’s side were level at half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans’ 44th-minute strike against the club he left last summer

Josh McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead with a penalty straight after the interval and the visitors looked on course for a big win when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Manchester United scored twice in injury-time – substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu with the goals – to salvage a point and avoid sitting joint-bottom during the international break.

Despite two comebacks, United’s current position is their lowest at this stage of a season since 1986, while their eight-game winless league run has only happened once before.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United finished the Aston Villa thriller with a back-four of Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Patrick Dorgu, and Neville said that line-up would struggle to avoid relegation to the Championship.

‘The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window,’ he said on NBC Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

‘The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in.

‘They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.’

Gary’s brother Phil, who also enjoyed incredible success at Manchester United as a player, added: ‘The back-four that finished the game – Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu – that gets you relegated.

"Should be banging heads!" 😡Roy Keane discusses how Manchester United can improve their form pic.twitter.com/r7JZzj62LD

‘That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League.

‘That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League.’

Despite Manchester United’s grim position in the Premier League, Gary Neville doubts a change in the dugout would improve the situation in the long-term.

‘You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce,’ he added. ‘When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again.

‘You can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years, that’s not the answer.

‘Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do.

‘It’s rinse and repeat. Amorim, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick – some of them are world class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex players who know the club as well.

‘None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you’ve got poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail.

‘Every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom – your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

‘There are real issues within that football club, you’ve got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.’

#1868. Michael Carrick speaks out on Diogo Dalot future after Manchester United fans make feelings clear

Manchester United fans made their frustrations with Diogo Dalot very clear at Old Trafford on Sunday, but Michael Carrick has defended the under-fire full-back.

The bizarre match finished 4-4 with Aston Villa, as the visitors twice relinquished a two-goal lead to their struggling hosts.

Alysson and Nicolas Jackson had put the Villains 2-0 up within five minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to put the Red Devils level by half-time.

Villa were two goals in front by 53 minutes as John McGinn and Leon Goretzka started the second half brilliantly and Old Trafford was stunned again.

However, Carrick’s men pulled off a remarkable escape in stoppage time as substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dourgu both scored after the 90-minute mark to rescue a point.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu replaced Dalot on 66 minutes after a nightmare performance from the Portugal international, which included conceding a penalty for felling Alysson, leading to McGinn’s goal from the spot.

When his number came up there were loud cheers from supporters at Old Trafford, which turned to boos as he left the field.

The 27-year-old has played in all 10 of Manchester United’s Premier League fixtures this season but when Carrick was asked if it was time for him to come out of the team, he pushed back and defended the full-back.

‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think,’ said the Red Devils boss.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I understand the frustration and the disappointment of the supporters. I get it, we’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed. The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played really well at times.

‘He gives the penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

‘He cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything. I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game that’s a whole different decision and that’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

Dalot signed for Manchester United in 2018 and has become something of a symbol of the mediocrity that fans have watched since then.

Gary Neville, who knows plenty about playing full-back for Manchester United, defended Dalot from criticism earlier this year, saying in January on his Sky Sports podcast: ‘He gets a really harsh view at times [from] quite a few United fans. I do think there’s a half-decent full-back in there, and I watch full-backs so closely.

‘I think he’s actually good in the air. I think he’s got good athleticism about him. I think he’s decent on the ball. I don’t think he’s a world-class full-back, but neither was I.’

He added: ‘I think he’s got something about him. I think he’s got 7/10 in him every single week, Dalot, but because we’ve seen him at left wing-back, we’ve seen him at right wing-back, we’ve seen him exposed so many times.

‘I think if he just played right full-back and played there all the time, I wouldn’t be getting rid of him in a hurry.

‘Now, other people might disagree with me, but I think I know the position of full-back, and I think he could do a decent job for Manchester United.’

Neville was not complimentary about the United defence on Sunday, though, saying on NBC Sports: ‘The reason that Manchester United have conceded four goals is they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window.

‘Everybody knew they had to invest in the defence. They needed defenders. They’re making mistake after mistake after mistake.’

The draw with Villa means Manchester United have won just one of their opening 10 games of the Premier League season and sit 18th in the table.

#1866. Michael Carrick told Man Utd star was ‘playing for himself’ in Aston Villa draw

Troy Deeney took aim at Amad Diallo following Manchester United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, claiming the winger ‘flattered to deceive’ and appeared to be ‘playing for himself’.

United twice fought back from two goals down to come away from Old Trafford with a point in Sunday’s thriller at Old Trafford, but the result saw Michael Carrick’s men enter the international break in the relegation zone.

The hosts were punished for their sluggishness early on as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson made it 2-0 inside only four minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to find the net and draw level.

The Red Devils were once again punished for a slow start, though, as John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty before Leon Goretzka capitalised on some calamitous defending from Leny Yoro to restore the visitors’ two-goal cushion.

Staring down the barrel of a fifth Premier League defeat, Carrick rang the changes in search of a route back into the contest in the second half – and it was two of United’s substitutes, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, who struck to salvage a draw at the death.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But with his side hovering just one point above rock-bottom Crystal Palace, Carrick will know the scrutiny and speculation surrounding his future is likely to rumble on ahead of the club’s crunch match away to bitter rivals Liverpool in a fortnight’s time.

‘I spoke about this on our last episode on Thursday, I feel like we’re doing the same things with Manchester United,’ ex-Watford and Birmingham striker Deeney said of United’s latest performance on talkSPORT’s Premier League All Access Podcast.

There had been calls for Carrick to field Shea Lacey in place of Amad following the youngster’s outstanding cameo display in United’s midweek Champions League victory over Roma.

However, the United head coach stuck to his guns and kept faith with Amad, who would go on to have a tough afternoon at the Theatre of Dreams.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Amad comes in and flatters to deceive,’ Deeney said of the Ivorian’s display.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘A lot of running into nothing, he was… today it felt like a lot of them were playing for themselves and going, “Look, I’m not the problem!”

‘Amad had about nine shots in the first half that were never going to be on target.’

On United’s problems in the centre of the park, Deeney continued: ‘I saw a midfield that was empty and vacated today.

‘Villa went through that midfield at will, many times in that first 75 minutes.’

Unai Emery made five substitutions before United’s late fightback, with goalscorers McGinn, Alysson, Goretzka and Jackson all removed, as well as the lively Johan Manzambi.

Asked whether the Villa manager had made a mistake with his changes, Deeney replied: ‘Absolutely.

‘I also thought it was one of the few times where he’d probably be very disappointed and would want to go back when you look at taking off Johan Manzambi, who I thought was excellent.

‘His ability to not only roll the player and keep the ball, but buy fouls and take them ten, 15, 20 yards up the pitch was excellent.

‘I think the game got too easy for Villa at 4-2 and I thought Emery started to think a little bit too far ahead, “Okay, I can rest these players”, obviously going away to international break.

‘Nicolas Jackson at times looked like Kylian Mbappe against that Manchester United team. He was dropping team, running in behind, he was 15 yards away from everyone.

‘But I just think he made too many mistakes and you can’t account for a goalkeeper having a shocker as well.’

Diogo Dalot appeared to be targeted with sarcastic cheers from the Old Trafford crowd when he was replaced for Dorgu midway through the second half.

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Carrick jumped to Dalot’s defence and encouraged supporters to get behind the players, especially when they are playing out of position.

‘Diogo, he gives absolutely everything,’ Carrick said.

‘He’s played in different positions, he’s played left-back, he’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today, that’s, you know, he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.’

On Dalot, the United boss went on: ‘I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

#1865. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta reveals "valuable" role amid Antonio Nusa links to Gunners ahead of January window

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 15:22

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed that international matches are used to help assess potential transfer targets amid links to Antonio Nusa.

The RB Leipzig winger has often been touted as a possible target of the Gunners, especially as the Londoners have at times looked blunt in the final third.

With the international break beginning after this weekend, the 21-year-old will be back in action for Norway, and he will play alongside Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard.

Speaking to reporters ahead of their Premier League clash with Hull City on Saturday, Arteta insisted that international matches can be informative when making transfer decisions, saying: "Yes, we do [use international football to aid work ahead of a transfer window].

"Obviously, when we have the opportunity to talk to our players about some players that they share two or three weeks together with, it's very valuable information. I think we all do that. It is a big difference between the Premier League and international football and what is there, but there's always a lot to learn."

Nusa has been included in the Norway squad for his nation's games against Wales on November 14 and against Demark on November 17, and perhaps Odegaard could help convince the winger to move to the Emirates in that time.

Nusa is enjoying a strong season in Germany, with the winger currently Leipzig's leading scorer (six) and assist provider (seven) in all competitions.

His return in both categories have already surpassed the five goals and four assists he produced in 2025-26, and his pace has proven deadly when cutting inside onto his right foot from the left flank.

It is rare for an attacker to be as strong at finishing as they are at creating chances, so Nusa's profile could be invaluable against deep defences.

While he is likely to be expensive in either the January or summer transfer windows, Arsenal should have him high on their radar.

Arsenal have at times been criticised for their style of play, with opposition fans and pundits arguing that they lack attacking intent.

However, it should be remembered that Arteta does not have a particularly elite set of forwards to choose from, with there question marks about every attacker's place in the lineup.

While Nusa may take time to settle into the Premier League, the prospect of Arsenal improving their frontline should be a worry for the rest of the division given the Gunners are already one of the best defensive teams in the world.
