#1822. Club Leon vs CD Guadalajara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 07 Nov 2026 23:56, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 18:04

Club Leon host CD Guadalajara, known as Chivas, in the Liga MX Apertura 2026 at Estadio Leon (Nou Camp) on Monday.

Leon sit ninth on 22 points in the Liga MX Apertura table after Friday's matches and need results to hold a top-eight place, while Chivas are already through to the quarter-finals on 29 points and are chasing the top seed with America and Cruz Azul level on the same total.

Leon have 22 points from 15 matches, built on six wins, four draws and five defeats, with a goal difference of only +2 from 22 scored and 20 conceded.

That leaves La Fiera ninth after Friday's round, level on points with eighth-placed Tijuana, who hold a better goal difference of +3, with Monterrey one point behind on 21 and Pumas and Queretaro on 20.

Javier Gandolfi's side have gone two matches without a win, drawing 1-1 with Toluca at home on October 24 and then losing 2-1 at Cruz Azul on November 1, where Andres Montano converted a 56th-minute penalty, Jose Paradela added a second in the 72nd minute and Jose Alvarado replied only with a stoppage-time penalty.

The 3-5 home defeat by America on October 17 is the clearest warning for this fixture, because it belongs to a run of nine goals conceded in the last five matches, in which Leon have scored every time, eight in total, and won only once, 2-0 at Tigres on October 20.

Leon won both league meetings with Chivas in 2025 at the Nou Camp, 2-1 on January 28 and 1-0 on July 19, and the fixture has not ended level at Estadio Leon since November 2016, but the most recent meeting was a 5-0 defeat at Estadio Akron on March 18.

Gandolfi said after the Cruz Azul defeat that Liguilla qualification depends only on his own team, and the arithmetic backs him up: a win would take Leon to 25 points, a draw to 23, and a defeat would leave them on 22 before the final-round trip to Santos Laguna.

Chivas have 29 points from 15 matches, with eight wins, five draws and two defeats, and their 14 goals conceded is the lowest total in the league, against 25 scored.

Gabriel Milito's side have won three in a row, 1-0 against Necaxa on October 20, 1-0 at Monterrey on October 24, where goalkeeper Raul Rangel saved a penalty, and 4-2 against Atlante on October 31, after a four-match winless run in which they collected three points from 12.

The Atlante win was led by 18-year-old Santiago Sandoval, who scored twice as a false nine after Milito left Angel Sepulveda and Ricardo Marin on the bench, with Efrain Alvarez adding one of his own and Diogo Bagui scoring an own goal.

Sandoval made his Liga MX debut as a substitute against Leon on July 19, 2025, scored both goals against Tigres in the Clausura quarter-finals, and he now has five league goals this tournament, level with Roberto Alvarado and Marin.

Chivas are the only team in the league without an away defeat, with three wins and four draws from seven road matches for 13 of 21 points, and both of their defeats this tournament came at the Estadio Akron.

America, Chivas and Cruz Azul are level on 29 points, with America ahead on a goal difference of +15 against Chivas' +11 and Cruz Azul's +10, and Chivas close the regular season at home to Cruz Azul on November 22.

Leon have no new injury concerns, although Jose Ramirez and Santiago Londono have been left out of Gandolfi's plans, while Luis Valadez (foot injury), and Angel Estrada (fractured tibia) are not available.

Juan Guevara is one yellow card from a suspension, which matters for a back line that has conceded 20 goals, and Sebastian Vegas is also reported to be on four bookings.

Gandolfi is expected to keep the side that started at Cruz Azul, with Panama international Ismael Diaz, Edgar Guerra and Alfonso Alvarado leading the attack.

For the visitors, Miguel Tapias remains in rehabilitation and Miguel Gomez has returned to treatment after a muscle relapse.

Luis Romo returned to the starting lineup against Atlante after a biceps femoris injury suffered on Mexico national-team duty, and Jose Castillo, Brian Gutierrez and Angel Sepulveda are back in contention.

Milito is expected to stay with the lineup that beat Atlante, although Marin, who has five league goals, and Sepulveda are the options if he restores a nominal striker in place of Sandoval's false-nine role.

Garcia; Moreno, Romana, Guevara, Mora; Echeverria, Rodriguez, Arcila; Guerra, A. Alvarado, Diaz

Rangel; Campillo, Romo, Aguirre; Ledezma, Govea, R. Gonzalez, B. Gonzalez; Alvarez, R. Alvarado, Sandoval

The gap in the numbers points towards Chivas, who average 1.67 goals per game against a Leon defence that concedes 1.33, while Leon must break down a Chivas back line that has conceded only 14 goals and kept six clean sheets.

Leon have scored in each of their last five league matches and won both previous league meetings at the Nou Camp in 2025, so a goal for the hosts is likely, but they have taken only five points from their last five games and conceded in 11 of their 15 matches, and we expect Chivas to score twice and leave Leon needing a result at Santos Laguna on the final day.

#1821. Why Do Football Clubs Let Players Leave for Free?

Why would a club let a valuable player walk out the door for nothing?

Because sometimes nothing is the best offer on the table.

Football clubs may let a player leave for free when the cost or risk of a new contract outweighs the value of keeping him.

A club may also prefer one final season of sporting contribution to a modest transfer fee. Sometimes the player chooses not to renew, while the signing club can still face wages, bonuses and agent fees.

So the word “free” does a lot of heavy lifting in football.

It is the only price tag in the sport that tells you what the selling club gets, and nothing about what the buying club pays.

This guide explains the topic for senior professional football, with examples drawn from English football.

Where FIFA rules and domestic rules part ways, we say so without hesitation.

A free transfer is a move in which no transfer fee is paid to the previous club, commonly because the player’s contract has expired.

When we’re talking about a free agent, we’re talking about an unattached player.

“Free” describes the absence of a transfer fee here. It does not remove wages, signing costs or any compensation that rules may still require.

The word also gets stretched quite a bit.

A contract that runs out on its end date is a free transfer. A deal that both sides agree to end early, called mutual termination, is something else. So is a release, where a club lets a player go while he is still under contract.

Headlines rarely make the distinction, but the rulebook does.

You can compare free signings with fee-paying moves in our confirmed football transfers database.

No sporting director wakes up planning to lose a player for nothing.

It happens when every other option looks worse, which in football is more often than fans like to believe.

Unless a club explains its motive in public (and clubs rarely do), read them as general reasoning, not as the known story behind any specific deal.

A renewal is rarely a copy of the old deal.

It usually comes with a raise, a signing bonus and a fresh agent fee. If the club doubts the player will be worth that money in year three or four, letting the contract expire is the cheaper mistake.

A lengthy contract for an older player can increase a club’s exposure to injury or declining performance.

The club pays the full salary whether the player stays fit or not, and many clubs would rather stop early.

A player who no longer fits still collects his wages, and those wages still count against the club’s spending limits. Loyalty does not have its own line in the accounts.

Sometimes a club lets a contract run out on purpose.

If the best offer is modest, one more season of goals, a title push or a cup run can be worth more than the money.

Fans may call it a blunder in January. By May, some of them call it a trophy.

A club cannot force a renewal and it cannot force a sale either.

If the player turns down every new contract and every move his club agrees, the deal simply runs out. He leaves for free, usually with a better offer already waiting somewhere else.

A short contract gives a club less long-term wage exposure and gives a player an earlier chance to renegotiate or move. It also offers less security to the player and less protection of resale value to the club. The right length depends on performance risk, bargaining power and each side’s plans.

For a club, a two-year deal limits the damage if a signing flops. The price is that the club may be shopping for a replacement sooner than planned.

It protects resale value, because any buyer must pay to take over the years still left. But it turns into an anchor if the player’s form drops, since the wages keep coming whether he plays or not.

Short contracts and free transfers are related, but they are not the same decision.

A short deal moves the end date closer. What happens on that date is a separate argument, usually held in a room full of agents.

Every contract has a clock on it, and the clock usually works for the player.

As a contract approaches expiry, a club will generally have less leverage in transfer negotiations, because the player may become available without a fee.

Is there a formula for how fast that value falls?

Form, demand, injuries and competition among interested clubs can all affect the fee available.

For clubs hoping to recover a transfer fee, an earlier sale or a contract extension may improve their position.

Keeping the player until expiry can still be the better sporting decision.

A player’s value and the cost of signing him are not necessarily the same thing. Transfer fees attract most of the headlines, while wages, signing bonuses and agent payments can be just as important to a club’s finances. Transfer speculation also extends beyond traditional football reporting, with discussions appearing on social media and platforms such as crypto betting site Sportbet.one, although these conversations should not be confused with verified transfer fees or the actual financial terms of a deal.

Before 1995, a player at the end of his contract was not really free.

His old club could still demand a fee before letting him go, and Jean-Marc Bosman, a Belgian midfielder, found that out in 1990.

He was nearing the end of his contract with RFC Liège and rejected a new offer that would have cut his salary by about 75%. He wanted to join French club Dunkerque instead.

The two clubs reached a conditional transfer agreement, but Liège doubted Dunkerque’s ability to pay and never requested the transfer certificate the move required. The deal fell through, and Liège suspended him.

He won five years later, and thousands of players have earned more from his case than he ever did.

The Bosman ruling of December 15, 1995 stopped clubs from demanding a fee for an out-of-contract player moving to a club in another EU member state.

It did not end every form of post-contract compensation worldwide, whatever the legend says.

When it comes to signings, FIFA’s rules set the timing.

Under article 18(3) of the FIFA Regulations on the Status and Transfer of Players (July 2025 edition), a player may sign with a new club once his contract has expired or is due to expire within six months.

The new club must first tell the current club in writing.

The six months count back from the real end date, so the magic month is not always January.

And signing a future contract is not the same as being registered to play.

Registration still depends on the transfer window and domestic rules.

The signing club may pay wages, a signing-on bonus and agent fees, even when no transfer fee goes to the previous club.

Compare the full contract period and separate one-off payments from annual pay before judging which deal costs less.

Illustrative five-year signing costs. Original SoccerNews editorial example using hypothetical figures, not a real transfer or market average.

Calculation: fee-paying = £20m + (5 × £3m) + £1m + £2m = £38m. Out-of-contract = £0 + (5 × £5m) + £5m + £3m = £33m. Annual wages are counted once, through the five-year total. Assumptions: both players complete five full years; wages are fixed gross amounts; bonuses and agent fees are paid by the signing club and counted once. Excludes employer payroll charges, taxes, performance bonuses, financing, add-ons, training compensation, resale income and early termination. These are nominal commitments, not cash schedules or accounting expenses.

In this hypothetical example, the free signing costs £33m over five years, compared with £38m for the fee-paying signing.

Higher wages and signing costs absorb much of the saved fee. Different contract terms could reverse the result.

In other words, the costs shift between transfer fees, wages and other signing expenses.

Which brings us to the most confusing pair of words in football. A free agent is the player. A football agent is the representative who negotiates for him, and sometimes for a club. Only one of those job titles contains the word “free.” Neither of them works for free.

Premier League clubs reported £460.3 million in payments to football agents for the period from February 4, 2025 to February 2, 2026, according to The FA.

The figure covers reported agent payments across different types of transactions, including some agreed before the reporting period. It should not be read as the cost of free transfers alone.

Premier League Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules in force for 2026/27 assess defined squad costs against relevant revenue and player-sale results.

The 85% Green Threshold operates alongside additional allowance and a Red Threshold, so crossing 85% does not automatically trigger a points deduction. Free signings still create relevant costs through pay and other deal expenses. (Premier League)

In plain terms, every pound spent on the squad now fights for the same space.

Squad costs include wages, agent fees and transfer fees spread over time, a process called amortization. Since the Premier League’s five-year rule for new or extended contracts, a fee can be spread over five years at most.

So a £20m fee on a five-year deal adds £4m a year to the accounts (£20m ÷ 5). This assumes straight-line accounting and no early sale or write-down. It is an accounting charge, not the cash payment, which can follow a different schedule.

In this example, an out-of-contract signing avoids the £4m annual amortization charge linked to the hypothetical £20m transfer fee. The club must still account for the player’s wages and any other signing or registration costs. That is the part of “free” the unveiling photo never shows.

You can follow how this plays out window by window in our Premier League transfers coverage.

A club that lets a player walk is not always being careless.

It weighs sporting value against the price of a renewal, and the player gets a vote too. For the signing club, “free” generally means no transfer fee to the previous club, not a cost-free deal.

Under FIFA’s July 2025 regulations, a professional may conclude a contract with another club when his current contract has expired or is due to expire within six months. The approaching club must first inform the current club in writing. Domestic rules and the regulatory edition in force must also be checked.

Some out-of-contract players can be registered outside a registration period under specified exceptions. Being unattached does not create an unlimited right to register at any time. The date the contract ended, association rules and competition eligibility all matter.

No transfer fee does not always mean no compensation. Training-compensation rules can apply to qualifying young players, and domestic schemes may also apply. Contract expiry is different from early termination, which can raise other compensation questions.

It is a one-off payment a club makes to a player for agreeing to join. A signing-on bonus may be substantial in a free transfer, but the amount depends on the negotiation.

No. A club can accept an offer, but the player must agree personal terms with the buyer. If he says no, he stays until his contract ends.

Rule summaries are based on the Bosman judgment (C-415/93), the FIFA Regulations on the Status and Transfer of Players (July 2025 edition), Premier League statements on squad-cost rules and amortization, and The FA’s 2025-26 agent-payment report. The cost table is an original SoccerNews example with hypothetical figures. Rules change, so check the edition in force on the date you read this. Browse more football explainers.

#1820. Celtic hierarchy deserve credit for fronting up at fan meeting... but the toughest questions still lie ahead for beleaguered boss Martin O'Neill

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:53 EST, 4 November 2026

It says much about where Celtic are as a club right now that very little of Martin O’Neill’s pre-match press conference actually centred on the match in question.

Just in case you hadn’t heard, Turkish giants Besiktas are in town for a game which the Parkhead men surely must win to stand any chance of progressing in the Europa League.

Their squad contains former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu and ex-Arsenal midfielder Leandro Trossard. For added spice, how about former Rangers’ defender Ridvan Yilmaz playing left-back, or Vaclav Cerny, a man who once squirted water at Celtic supporters, being their right-winger?

Their manager, Vincenzo Italiano, also happened to oversee Bologna in January as O’Neill’s men emerged with a draw from a fiery encounter on the road.

On another day, those plot lines would have dominated the agenda. Yet they were relegated to mere footnotes as a consequence of Celtic’s seemingly inexorable lurch towards crisis point.

Bluntly, the identity of the side which will seek to inflict a record fifth consecutive European defeat on their team is of little concern right now to the green and white hordes. They only see a side which is regressing and a manager and a backroom staff who seem incapable of arresting the slide.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill is hoping a much-needed win in Europe can help lift the gloom

More significantly, in the wider picture, they view the hierarchy as being devoid of the necessary ambition or footballing intelligence to turn the tanker around. The lack of scrutiny the directors have subjected themselves to as matters have steadily deteriorated on their watch is another major bugbear.

Purely taken in isolation, then, it’s hard to be critical of the fact that some of those suited figures – plus O’Neill – voluntarily put themselves through a ‘hard but fair’ questioning at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening.

‘When things are going really well at the football club, you can take all the plaudits and all that you want,’ said the manager. ‘At the end of the day, there are bad times and I think that you should face up to that.’

O’Neill, to be clear, wasn’t on the original list to attend. Once he heard of the event, he made it his business to be there.

While he could have lived without a balaclava-clad welcoming committee, he felt the exercise was largely positive.

‘First of all, I wasn’t really aware of the meeting, so it was kind of an ad hoc thing,’ he explained.

‘I spoke to Michael (Nicholson, chief executive) and he said that they were going to meet. And I said, “Well, I wouldn’t mind going down to it if that was the case”, obviously to experience what the fans would be asking.

Falkirk's defeat of the champions last weekend has seen a wave of criticism hit the Celtic boss

‘I don’t know whether they expected me to be there or not, but it doesn’t really matter. Regardless of who was there, the meeting itself was robust with strong, strong questioning.

‘Hopefully, some of the answers would maybe quell if not satisfy. I don’t know what the overall picture would be. But, yeah, I was pleased to have gone.’

Accused of adopting the public profiles of Invisible Men throughout this year, the presence of Nicholson, Chris McKay and Brian Wilson in Inverclyde became instantly newsworthy.

With the divide between the boardroom and fans apparently widening by the week, even hardened cynics viewed the trip to the Tail O’ The Bank as a small step in the right direction.

With the AGM on the horizon, the hope is that the meeting might just lead to a more civilised discourse going forward.

By all accounts, the questions asked on every subject from recruitment to the hoarding of cash were answered as fully as possible. But no one on the floor left the building clicking their heels at what the future holds. Talk is cheap, after all.

‘If the takeaway was that the board were going to do something to satisfy the supporters in that sense, then that would be great,’ added O’Neill. ‘That would be brilliant for all.’

Angry Celtic supporters continue to make their feelings clear on the club's board every week

By sheer chance, O’Neill was scheduled to attend a Q&A with supporters when he first returned to the club last year. A Celtic legend as a consequence of his exploits at the turn of the century, those present stopped just short of carrying him in a sedan chair.

After just three wins in ten games, the mood music around him was a little less jovial in Greenock.

For perhaps the first time in his long association with the club, adverse results have seen a spotlight shine on him.

‘That’s the course of a football season or the experiences of a football club,’ he shrugged. ‘I think sometimes you have to put a few things into perspective, both good and bad. And I think the other night was one of those, you know?

‘People are asking me now if it’s something I’m going to continue to do. No, my main job depends on results and winning some football matches. That’s the most important thing.’

Back in the day, criticism over such a wretched run would have been limited to newspaper columns and radio phone-ins. In the modern era, the level of flak is amplified by the proliferation of podcasts and blogs from citizen journalists.

‘I have never been immune to that,’ O’Neill insisted. ‘Listen, everyone would love to be praised every single minute of your life. But that’s not going to happen. You’ve got to forget about the noise and try and get on with it and get back to winning ways.

Former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu will lead the line for Besiktas at Parkhead on Thursday

‘Everyone is a tactician now, that’s the whole point. Everybody is a football manager. There are people who have got jobs in football now because they played a PlayStation. Honestly, it’s extraordinary. But it does not bother me, honestly, it doesn’t.

‘People talk about tactics, but in my semi-defence, no one talked about tactics when we won the seven games to win the league. Or the 14 games we won before we got beat.

‘And you know what? If you got beaten in a game, you think that maybe that somebody has out-thought you. Absolutely. You’re right to think that.

‘John McGlynn has every right to be proud of his (Falkirk) side after beating us and to have had the upper hand.’

O’Neill, unusually, has got used to losing lately, with seven reverses coming by the first week in November. But, as those in attendance on Monday or when he appeared in Dingwall for a B team game the following night will attest, he’s not lost his desire to lead or to win. He remains all-in.

‘I really have to be, honestly, because I’m supposed to be the driver of the club,’ he stated.

‘For instance, last night (Tuesday), that was wildly important for me to go up to that game (in Dingwall). I feel that that’s my job at the end of the day.’

#1819. Sunday's Premier League predictions including Man Utd vs. Aston Villa, Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Premier League predictions include Manchester United at home to Aston Villa, before struggling Crystal Palace take on Liverpool.

High-flying Brighton & Hove Albion will welcome Brentford to the Amex Stadium for Sunday's Premier League encounter.

The Seagulls head into the weekend in third spot in the Premier League table, while the Bees start matchday 10 in sixth position.

Brighton have scored at least three goals in each of their five competitive home wins this season, and while Brentford have drawn all four of their away league games this term, we think the Seagulls will make full use of their firepower to extend their unbeaten head-to-head home run with a relatively comfortable victory.

Ipswich Town play host to Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon looking for the win that could catapult them into the top half of the Premier League table.

While the Tractor Boys start the next batch of fixtures in 14th position, the Cherries are in eighth place after three successive victories in the top flight.

Ipswich will feel that their lighter schedule and week off from action gives them a clear advantage for this contest. However, we cannot back against a Bournemouth side who are free-scoring and searching for their eighth successive victory in all competitions.

Liverpool will hope to bounce back and deliver a fatal blow to Pierre Sage's hopes of remaining in charge of Crystal Palace when the two clash in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds are sixth in the top flight with 15 points after nine matchweeks, and the come into the weekend on the back of a 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, whereas Palace are 18th with just seven points and could end the weekend in last place.

Palace may boast the advantage of playing at home, but their lack of options in attack could cost them.

While Liverpool have been far from perfect in the final third, they have often taken three points from Selhurst Park, and it would not be surprising if they claimed another victory on the road this weekend.

Needing nothing short of a minor miracle to replicate their 2025-26 feats against Chelsea, Sunderland host the Blues in Sunday's Premier League fixture at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats trail their visitors by 16 places and 11 points in the Premier League table at the time of writing and face Xabi Alonso's well-rested men after a sobering defeat in Europe too.

Fatigue should not play a significant role for Sunderland on Sunday given the alterations Le Bris made in midweek, but backing the Black Cats to get anything out of any Premier League game at present is a tough ask.

Therefore, even a Pedro-less Chelsea side - working on a full week's worth of rest - should stroll to victory, with an increasingly familiar clean sheet in tow.

Desperate to steer clear of the Premier League's relegation zone, Manchester United will host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

The Red Devils are hoping to build on their midweek Champions League victory, while the Lions are keen to get back on track after a three-game winless run.

Man United may have won in midweek, but they were the beneficiaries of major errors from the Roma defence, and are unlikely to repeat the feat on Sunday.

Villa are on a three-game winless run that has spanned three different competitions, yet they will be optimistic about getting the better of their struggling hosts.

#1817. Sunday's Serie A predictions including Napoli vs. Lazio, Inter Milan vs. Como

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 08 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Serie A predictions cover an intriguing round of fixtures, with AC Milan travelling to Genoa, Juventus visiting Fiorentina and Atalanta BC taking on Monza, while Napoli host Lazio and defending champions Inter Milan welcome Como to the San Siro.

Trending in very different directions, Serie A leaders Lazio will visit a faltering Napoli side on Sunday, as Stadio Maradona hosts the lunchtime kickoff.

While the home side are struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, their southern rivals have posted nine wins from 10 and are yet to taste defeat in the league.

Struggling in Serie A, facing another early exit from Europe and burdened by a huge absence list, Napoli are set to lose three games on the spin.

While Lazio's stellar run will surely end soon, they can exploit their hosts' shaky defence and post a seventh straight win.

Atalanta BC will be looking to end a six-match winless run across all competitions when they travel to Monza on Sunday for matchday 11 of the Serie A campaign.

Maurizio Sarri's side sit 13th in the Italian top-flight table after collecting just 11 points from their opening 10 matches, leaving them four points above the relegation zone, where the hosts occupy 18th place.

Monza's defensive problems make it difficult to see them containing Atalanta, who have dominated this fixture in recent years, and that could provide the visitors with a good opportunity to end their current winless run.

After a week of highs and lows, AC Milan will head towards the international break with a tough trip to Genoa on Sunday afternoon.

Before they clash at Stadio Ferraris, the hosts have actually claimed more points from their last five Serie A games than the inconsistent Rossoneri.

Allied to two cup wins at Stadio Ferraris, Genoa have won half of their first six home games in Serie A, so Milan will be put through a stern test.

While Amorim's men are leaking too many goals, De Rossi's side have found their shooting boots, and that could produce an end-to-end draw.

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter Milan must try to get back on track when they welcome record-breaking Como to San Siro on Sunday.

Following four intense meetings last term, the regional rivals are currently separated by two points, with both trailing surprise leaders Lazio.

Inter's defence is creaking at the seams, and without the leadership of their inspirational skipper they are always more vulnerable.

Although free-flowing Como must be starting to tire, recent events suggest it is time to finally slay the Nerazzurri.

Sending Serie A into the international break, old foes Fiorentina and Juventus will clash at Stadio Franchi on Sunday night.

While the Viola are still seeking their first home win of the season, fallen giants Juve have been left trailing Italy's top six.

Both teams have been too inconsistent to match their pre-season aims, making the outcome on Sunday night quite tough to predict.

Juve are assured of a hostile reception in Florence, but the hosts tend to wilt in front of their own fans - so, all three points will go back to Turin.

#1816. Atletico Madrid willing to wait for Alvarez to hit form

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Diego Simeone is willing to be patient with Julian Alvarez, who he feels is vital to getting Atletico Madrid to where they want to be.

Alvarez has netted just twice in all competitions this season, while providing three assists.

His latest goal involvement came on Sunday, as he teed up Giuliano Simeone to open the scoring against Barcelona. The Blaugrana, though, went on to win 2-1.

Barca pushed hard to sign Alvarez this past summer, with Atletico refusing to budge and even threatening legal action against the reigning LaLiga champions.

And though Alvarez is yet to hit his peak form, Simeone is willing to wait.

"He's an extraordinary player, we love him dearly, we need him, we need the best Julian, and we're going to work with him," the Atletico boss told Movistar+.

"Of the team's five good scoring opportunities, he was involved in three or four. He just lacked the goal that would have made him stand out, but it will come."

In his post-match press conference, Simeone added of Alvarez: "We all wish he had scored, but we'll wait for him; we need him because if we want to get where we want to go, we need him, otherwise we won't get there."

Asked if Alvarez was suffering from a lack of confidence, Simeone replied: "I'm not in his body, he has our trust."

— Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) November 9, 2026

Alvarez led Atletico for shots (four), touches in the opposition box (seven) and successful dribbles (three), while also creating two chances.

Atletico's defeat snapped a seven-game winning run in LaLiga. They sit third, two points behind second-place Real Madrid and five adrift of leaders Barca.

"I'm left with an outstanding performance from the players, nothing to complain about," Simeone told reporters.

"We put the opposing players in a position where they weren't comfortable. We lacked the clinical finishing we've shown on other occasions, and they're a very confident opponent who capitalised on their chances.

"I'm proud of the lads, I loved it, and I'm very happy with everyone's performance."

By Anthony Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 00:05, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:05

Today's Bundesliga predictions will have a major impact at both ends of the table, with Freiburg vying to keep their unlikely title challenge alive against Union Berlin, Bayer Leverkusen battling for Europe at FC Koln, and Schalke 04 desperate for points at Hoffenheim.

Bayer Leverkusen travel to FC Koln's RheinEnergieSTADION on Sunday and will hope to avoid falling behind in the race for a spot in the Bundesliga's top four.

The hosts are 14th in the table with nine points from a possible 24, whereas Leverkusen are in sixth place with 13 points following their 4-2 loss against Stuttgart on October 31.

Leverkusen's form of late has been concerning, though they have been difficult to beat when playing on the road.

Koln have been strong at RheinEnergieSTADION, and while they may struggle to get the better of the visitors, they should have enough to earn a point.

A rebalanced Freiburg will welcome relegation-threatened Union Berlin to Europa-Park Stadion on Sunday, hoping to keep their unlikely Bundesliga title challenge alive.

Die Breisgau-Brasilianer are searching for a fourth win on the bounce, while Die Eisernen are eyeing a first victory in five games.

Freiburg have rediscovered their form after a brief blip, and will be confident of taking all three points against one of the bottom three on Sunday.

Die Kraichgauer are looking for a first win in four games, while Die Knappen are desperate to avoid a fifth defeat in six matches.

Hoffenheim have struggled once again in recent weeks, but they will be quietly confident about their chances of beating one of the division's relegation favourites on Sunday.

Schalke's troubles in front of goal are well-documented, and it would be a surprise to see them find the back of the net, never mind walk away with anything from this clash.

#1812. Alisson FUMES at Liverpool team-mate Jeremy Jacquet after Reds star turned his back and deflected Mason Greenwood's free-kick beyond goalkeeper

Published: 14:15 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 18:19 EST, 4 November 2026

Alisson is usually composure personified for Liverpool but lost his rag with Jeremy Jacquet on Wednesday night.

The Brazilian gave his team-mate both barrels after Fenerbahce's equaliser - a heavily deflected Mason Greenwood free-kick.

Jacquet was at the edge of the Liverpool wall and twisted his body to take evasive action, with the ball ricocheting off his midriff and past the goalkeeper.

Jacquet has been a shining light for the Reds in his debut campaign but it was a poor moment that left his stopper livid.

Replay footage showed Greenwood's powerful attempt appeared to be heading wide before the deflection off Jacquet completely changed the trajectory.

Alisson had been moving swiftly to his left before being wrong-footed and the ball flew off the wet surface to his other side.

Alisson was raging at Jeremy Jacquet's poor blocking attempt for the Fenerbahce equaliser

Jacquet's expression indicated he knew he'd made a poor mistake for the goal

The 34-year-old's fury was immediate and he screamed at Jacquet, gesticulating wildly in his direction.

The centre-back appeared to recognise his mistake and brought his hand up to cover his eyes on a grim evening in Istanbul.

On commentary for TNT Sports, Ally McCoist said: 'It's Jacquet and he's livid (Alisson), does he turn his back? He certainly does, you've got to face it.

'The goalkeeper is livid, absolutely livid and with justification as well. He's (Jacquet) is side on for someone who has had a good start to the season.'

Jacquet has been partnering Virgil van Dijk in almost every game so far this term for Andoni Iraola's men and acquitted himself excellently.

Having joined from Rennes in the summer for £55million after agreeing the move in January, he's seamlessly replaced Ibrahima Konate, who left on a free transfer before signing for Real Madrid.

Jacquet is still just 21 and the France international will no doubt want to avoid the ire of his goalkeeper and learn his lesson when it comes to forming a solid wall.

Trey Nyoni had opened the scoring for the Reds before Greenwood's leveller. Alexander Isak then came off the bench to give the visitors the lead once more before Fenerbahce roared back.

Two goals in the space of six minutes gave the Turkish side a 3-2 lead in the pouring rain, to the delight of interim boss and cult Liverpool legend Dirk Kuyt and the home side held on for a famous win.

#1811. Burn replaces injured Guehi in England squad

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Marc Guehi has pulled out of England's squad due to injury, with Dan Burn replacing the centre-back in the squad.

Guehi was taken off at half-time in Manchester City's 3-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

He has now withdrawn from the Three Lions' squad for their upcoming Nations League contests against Croatia and world champions Spain.

Burn, who was one of England's standout performers when they beat Mexico in the World Cup in July, has been called up in Guehi's place.

Dan Burn has been added to Thomas Tuchel's #ThreeLions squad following the withdrawal of Marc Guéhi through injury.

The 34-year-old was absent from England's squad in September due to injury, but was then originally omitted by Tuchel for these fixtures, with Jarrad Branthwaite, Ezri Konsa, Ben White and Jarell Quansah given the nod.

Burn has made 11 appearances for England, with seven of those coming from the bench. He has played a part in four clean sheets.

Guehi, meanwhile, will see his run of playing in consecutive England matches come to an end at 15 appearances.

England sit second in Nations League Group A3, having won three of their four fixtures, losing only to Spain.

A point against Croatia on Thursday will be enough to see Tuchel's team into the quarter-finals.

#1810. CM: Amorim let down again in another European debacle – the players whose stock has dropped

There are several players that are at risk of slipping down Ruben Amorim’s pecking order with displays like the one against Ferencvaros.

Calciomercato.com write that three clues add up to mean that we can say with certainty that Milan are not aiming to win the Europa League despite being one of the favourites, at least on paper. The defeats against Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros were determined by two factors.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the attitude of the squad’s key players and the inadequacy of several reserves. The dominant Adrien Rabiot, for example, seems to sink when the Europa League anthem is played. The Frenchman – captain on this occasion due to Mike Maignan’s suspension – wasn’t the only culprit, but was certainly the most obvious.

The thing squad assembled last summer by Gerry Cardinale, Amorim and the management features a strong starting eleven that can compete with anyone (as was the case in the derby), but at the same time lacks alternatives.

In several cases, it’s fair to say that the players aren’t up to the task. Filippo Terracciano’s role is emblematic: already rejected by the previous management, he remained with Milan at Amorim’s request.

His season included 45 poorly played minutes against Benfica before being substituted at half-time, a straight red card as a substitute against Salzburg, and a poor performance against Ferencvaros that drew boos from the crowd.

Doubts are also growing over Ardon Jashari, who – after a few performances that were at least adequate – continues to display obvious technical and tactical limitations. The money spent on him (over €30m) is leading many to run out of patience.

The excellent performances against RB Salzburg and Udinese seemed to have reintroduced a courageous and powerful version of Davide Bartesaghi to Milan, but the most recent test saw him revert to the flaws of last season in terms of personality and concentration.

Pervis Estupinan, on the other hand, seems to have completely disappeared from the radar, having remained on the bench for the entire match against Ferencvaros. The two left-backs have a lot of work to do, and this could influence some transfer choices too.

#1809. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

#MUNMCI – 23'The referee's call of red card to Foden for violent conduct was checked and confirmed by VAR.REF: "Red card Phil Foden – kick out into the body of Bruno".VAR: "That looks like a clear red card to me. Looks to be a secondary movement. Confirming the red card for…

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

"THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE" banner above the tunnel#MUFC pic.twitter.com/hrs71K7r1y

Probably keeping the emotions away, which is not easy. It’s just try to embrace the chaos, that’s it..

I say chaos, [but] it can be noise. Embrace it, it’s a derby, it’s nice... Try to play our game!

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. We understand how important this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

If you haven’t checked out the interview, you can have a read here

Fans have chanted: “You treat us like s--- Ratcliffe and the Glazers, you treat us like s---.”

Some supporters also targeted ambitions to build a new 100,000 capacity stadium adjacent to Old Trafford by singing: “You can shove your new ground up your a---.”

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”

"An absolute WORLDIE from range!"Lewis Dunk scores a contender for goal of the season 🤯 pic.twitter.com/m5bPzm5Wm3

Struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

There are hundreds upon hundreds of #MUFC supporters pouring through the Munich tunnel protesting against the Glazers and Ratcliffe's ownership and running of the club pic.twitter.com/VlhkMoxbmI

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

Manchester City XI: Donnarumma, Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, Haaland

#1807. Prediction: Ivory Coast vs Gambia

Ivory Coast and Gambia will meet at Stade de la Paix in Bouake on Thursday, November 12, as the two early leaders in Group C continue their qualification campaigns for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

Both teams have collected six points from their opening two matches. Ivory Coast has done so without conceding, while Gambia arrives after scoring six goals against Somalia and Ghana.

Verdict: Over 2.5 goals Best odds: 16/25 Bookmaker: 1xBet

Ivory Coast has made a convincing start to qualifying, beating Ghana and Somalia by the same 2-0 scoreline. Those results have put the Elephants in a strong position before a pair of matches against their closest challenger.

Gambia has already won away to Ghana and has enough attacking quality to cause problems if the home side commits too many players forward.

Still, Ivory Coast has several ways to stretch the visiting defense. Amad Diallo, Nicolas Pepe and Yan Diomande give Renard options out wide, where beating the first defender could force Gambia’s central players out of position.

That should be an important part of the home side’s approach. Moving the ball quickly between the wings would make it harder for Gambia to protect the middle and give Ivory Coast opportunities to deliver into the penalty area.

The Elephants won the most recent meeting 1-0 in March 2025. Their opening qualifying results also suggest they can manage a game without allowing much at the other end.

However, Gambia’s attacking form gives this meeting a different feel. Ivory Coast may need to keep looking for goals even after taking the lead.

Renard has confirmed that Amad Diallo is fit following the injury concern that forced him off during his club’s match on October 31.

Odilon Kossounou and Guela Doue are absent from the squad. Evan Ndicka, Ousmane Diomande and Emmanuel Agbadou remain available in central defense, while Oumar Solet is among the new additions to the group.

Franck Kessie and Ibrahim Sangare offer experience in midfield, with Malick Yalcouye another option.

Further forward, Renard can choose from Amad, Pepe, Yan Diomande, Bazoumana Toure and Martial Godo, alongside central attacking options Elye Wahi and Bonny.

There is enough variety to change the attack during the match, particularly if Gambia manages to close the spaces around its penalty area.

Gambia’s opening results deserve attention. The Scorpions began with a 2-1 victory over Somalia before producing a 4-2 comeback win away to Ghana.

That second performance showed how dangerous this team can be when a match opens up. Gambia trailed 2-0 in Accra before Mohamed Badamosi and Omar Colley brought it level before halftime. Ebrima Colley then scored twice after the break to complete the turnaround.

Recovering from that position should give Johnathan McKinstry’s players confidence heading into another difficult away assignment. They have already shown that falling behind does not have to end their chances.

The defensive side of those performances is worth considering, though. Gambia conceded against Somalia and allowed Ghana to establish a two-goal lead. Similar lapses in Bouake could prove expensive.

McKinstry will probably want his midfield to stay close to the defense while leaving enough support for counterattacks. Sitting too deep for long periods would invite repeated pressure from Ivory Coast’s wide players.

There should be opportunities to break when the hosts push forward. Whether Gambia can use those moments effectively may determine how competitive this match becomes.

Gambia has been boosted by the return of Musa Barrow and Yankuba Minteh, who missed the opening two qualifiers through injury.

Their availability gives McKinstry additional attacking options alongside Ebrima Colley and Badamosi, both of whom contributed to the successful start.

However, Jesper Ceesay and Suleiman Camara have subsequently withdrawn because of injuries. Saidou Khan and Salieu Drammeh have been called up as their replacements.

Alieu Fadera is also unavailable with a thigh injury. Omar Colley offers experience in defense, while Ebou Adams and Abubakarr Barry are among the midfield options.

The returning attackers should help Gambia carry a threat beyond its own half. McKinstry will need that outlet if his team spends long stretches defending.

Ivory Coast should create enough chances to put Gambia’s defense under sustained pressure. The visitors have conceded in both qualifiers, and recovering from another poor start would be difficult against this opposition.

Gambia also has reasons to believe it can contribute to the scoring. Six goals in two qualifiers, followed by the return of Barrow and Minteh, give the away side a credible attacking threat.

Another controlled 2-0 home win is the main concern for this selection. Even so, the attacking options available and Gambia’s defensive vulnerabilities make over 2.5 goals the preferred bet.

Verdict: Over 2.5 goals Best odds: 16/25 Bookmaker: 1xBet

#1805. Man United could match shocking 73-year Arsenal feat in Aston Villa Premier League clash

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 07:36

Manchester United will be at risk of matching an unwanted feat last suffered by Arsenal 73 years ago when they take on Aston Villa in Sunday's Premier League finale.

The Red Devils welcome the Lions to Old Trafford after sinking to a new 40-year low, having dropped into the bottom three of the Premier League table on Saturday.

Nottingham Forest's 3-1 win over Manchester City saw the Tricky Trees leapfrog Michael Carrick's side, who are now two points adrift of safety in 18th position.

Not since 1986 have Man United found themselves in the bottom three after nine rounds of a top-flight season, and Carrick's side must win to overtake 17th-placed Coventry City on Sunday.

Should the Red Devils fail to claim all three points against Aston Villa, they would not only enter the international break in the relegation zone, but also join the worst kind of exclusive club.

Indeed, only three teams in English top-flight history have won just one of their opening 10 games of a season, after finishing in the top three of the standings the year before.

The last team to suffer that fate was Arsenal, who won just one of their first 10 matches in the 1953-54 First Division, after clinching the title in the 1952-53 campaign; the Gunners ultimately finished 12th that year.

Meanwhile, the Chelsea team of 1919-20 ranked third in the top flight, before opening the 1920-21 season with just one win from their opening 10 games en route to an 18th-placed finish.

The first - and only other club - to endure such a miserable starting run after a standout campaign the previous year was the 1894-95 Derby County side, but Man United are just 90 minutes away from entering that unwanted list.

Carrick has overseen just one win from Man Utd's first nine Premier League games in 2026-27 - alongside four draws and four losses - and the Red Devils are winless in seven top-flight clashes since thumping Ipswich Town 5-2 on August 30.

More unwanted history is on the line for the 20-time English champions on Sunday afternoon, when they could also open a season with just one win in 10 games for the first time in their Premier League history.

The Red Devils have not started a season so poorly since 1972-73, when they won one, drew four and lost five of their first 10, and only once before have they gone eight Premier League games without victory.

That occurrence happened a little over 12 months ago in April/May 2025 under Ruben Amorim, although that sequence coincidentally ended with a 2-0 win over Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

However, Carrick's men are still waiting for their first clean sheet of the Premier League season, also marking the first time in 40 years that they have gone nine games without a shut-out in a top-flight term.
